1	import AppKit
2	
3	/// The timeline's half of the selected action (spec §11 CI-1, CI-4): each
4	/// clip's ACTION LANE directly under its name strip, the band hit, the
5	/// selected span's wash down the clip body, and its shade on the ruler.
6	///
7	/// Extensions rather than lines in `TimelineView.swift`, which is frozen at
8	/// wiring (app/CLAUDE.md): the frozen file keeps one call in `hit(at:)`, one
9	/// in the ruler's `draw`, and `TimelineClipDrawing.swift` the two calls in a
10	/// clip's paint order — the wash before the name strip, the bands after it.
11	extension TimelineContentView {
12	    /// The lane: the top of the clip's content rect (under the name strip),
13	    /// full clip width, `DS.actionLaneHeights` tall at S/M/L — never taller
14	    /// than the content it sits in.
15	    static func actionLane(content: CGRect, sizeIndex: Int) -> CGRect {
16	        let heights = DS.actionLaneHeights
17	        let height = heights[min(max(sizeIndex, 0), heights.count - 1)]
18	        return CGRect(
19	            x: content.minX, y: content.minY, width: content.width,
20	            height: min(height, content.height))
21	    }
22	
23	    /// One action's band in the lane: its span, by CLIP time mapped back
24	    /// through the clip's own start, at least 2 pt wide.
25	    static func bandRect(
26	        _ a: ActionSnapshot, clip: ClipSnapshot, lane: CGRect, layout: TimelineLayout
27	    ) -> CGRect {
28	        let from = layout.x(for: clip.start + a.start)
29	        let to = layout.x(for: clip.start + a.endTime)
30	        return CGRect(x: from, y: lane.minY, width: max(to - from, 2), height: lane.height)
31	    }
32	
33	    /// The action whose band holds `point` — the LANE only, so a press on the
34	    /// clip body below it is still the clip. `hit(at:)` asks after the fade
35	    /// handles, which on an audio-only clip sit inside this lane and are
36	    /// painted over it, and before the edge grabs. Where bands overlap (the
37	    /// 2 pt minimum width, or a hand-written project) the LAST holding the
38	    /// point in `ActionBands.ordered` order wins, because bands paint in that
39	    /// order and it is the one on top — the Clip tab lane's `bandHit` rule. A
40	    /// zero-length band is never painted here, so unlike the lane it is never
41	    /// hit.
42	    func actionBandHit(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, rect: CGRect, at point: CGPoint) -> UInt32? {
43	        guard let owner = timeline else { return nil }
44	        let lane = Self.actionLane(
45	            content: Self.contentRect(rect), sizeIndex: owner.trackHeightIndex)
46	        guard lane.height > 0, lane.contains(point) else { return nil }
47	        return ActionBands.ordered(clip).last { action in
48	            action.duration > 0
49	                && Self.bandRect(action, clip: clip, lane: lane, layout: owner.layout)
50	                    .contains(point)
51	        }?.id
52	    }
53	
54	    /// What a press at `point` grabs on the clip's action lane: a band's grip
55	    /// (`.actionEdge`) or its body (`.action`), or nil off every band. The
56	    /// band is `actionBandHit`'s, unchanged; the grip is asked of that band's
57	    /// own rect (spec §11 CI-11).
58	    func actionHit(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, rect: CGRect, at point: CGPoint) -> TimelineHit? {
59	        guard let owner = timeline, let id = actionBandHit(clip, rect: rect, at: point),
60	              let action = clip.actions.first(where: { $0.id == id })
61	        else { return nil }
62	        let lane = Self.actionLane(
63	            content: Self.contentRect(rect), sizeIndex: owner.trackHeightIndex)
64	        let band = Self.bandRect(action, clip: clip, lane: lane, layout: owner.layout)
65	        if let edge = ActionBands.gripEdge(in: band, at: point.x) {
66	            return .actionEdge(clip: clip.id, action: id, edge)
67	        }
68	        return .action(clip: clip.id, action: id)
69	    }
70	
71	    /// The selected span down the whole clip body: the action ink at 12 %
72	    /// with 1 pt ends at 55 %. Drawn before the name strip, so the strip
73	    /// still reads over it.
74	    func drawActionWash(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, body: CGRect, owner: TimelineView) {
75	        guard let id = owner.selectedAction,
76	              let action = clip.actions.first(where: { $0.id == id })
77	        else { return }
78	        let layout = owner.layout
79	        let from = layout.x(for: clip.start + action.start)
80	        let to = layout.x(for: clip.start + action.endTime)
81	        let span = CGRect(x: from, y: body.minY, width: max(to - from, 2), height: body.height)
82	        DS.action.withAlphaComponent(0.12).setFill()
83	        span.fill()
84	        DS.action.withAlphaComponent(0.55).setFill()
85	        NSRect(x: span.minX, y: span.minY, width: 1, height: span.height).fill()
86	        NSRect(x: span.maxX - 1, y: span.minY, width: 1, height: span.height).fill()
87	    }
88	
89	    /// The lane's black-22 % backing and every band on it, numbered in time
90	    /// order, then — from M, on a clip whose rate moves — the rate line over
91	    /// them, inset 2 pt top and bottom (spec §11 SR-26). The backing is drawn
92	    /// only on a clip that has an action with a length (road map 9 §2's
93	    /// deviation: the handoff draws it on every clip).
94	    func drawActionBands(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, rect: CGRect, owner: TimelineView) {
95	        guard clip.actions.contains(where: { $0.duration > 0 }) else { return }
96	        let lane = Self.actionLane(
97	            content: Self.contentRect(rect), sizeIndex: owner.trackHeightIndex)
98	        guard lane.height > 0 else { return }
99	        NSColor.black.withAlphaComponent(0.22).setFill()
100	        lane.fill()
101	        let level = ActionBands.Level(sizeIndex: owner.trackHeightIndex)
102	        let graph = level == .bars ? nil : RateGraph.points(
103	            owner.sourceMaps(clip.id), in: lane.insetBy(dx: 0, dy: 2),
104	            x: { owner.layout.x(for: clip.start + $0) })

3	/// Retiming an action by dragging its band in the Clip tab's lane (spec §11
4	/// CI-11) — the same `ActionDragSession` the timeline drags with, through the
5	/// binding's live trio, so a drag is ONE undo step.
6	///
7	/// The lane selects at mouse-UP, not at the press as the timeline does: a
8	/// selection rebuilds the pane, and the pane must not rebuild under the
9	/// pointer (`refresh(isLive:)` skips rebuilds only while a live edit runs).
10	/// A click and a drop therefore share one path, `releaseBand`.
11	extension ActionLaneView {
12	    /// The clip time under `x`: the lane's fraction of the clip's length,
13	    /// clamped to the clip.
14	    func clipTime(atX x: CGFloat) -> Ticks {
15	        guard let clip = clip, clip.duration > 0 else { return 0 }
16	        let lane = laneRect
17	        guard lane.width > 0 else { return 0 }
18	        let fraction = min(max((x - lane.minX) / lane.width, 0), 1)
19	        return Ticks((Double(fraction) * Double(clip.duration)).rounded())
20	    }
21	
22	    /// The band under `point` and the grip it is in, if any. The LAST band
23	    /// holding the point wins, because bands paint in time order and that is
24	    /// the one on top — so a zero-length band sitting on another's start is
25	    /// the one a press takes. A zero-length band answers too (it is
26	    /// selectable), always with no edge: 2 pt is all body.
27	    func bandHit(at point: CGPoint) -> ActionBandHover? {
28	        guard let clipID, let band = bandRects().last(where: { $0.rect.contains(point) })
29	        else { return nil }
30	        return ActionBandHover(
31	            clip: clipID, action: band.id, edge: ActionBands.gripEdge(in: band.rect, at: point.x))
32	    }
33	
34	    /// Mouse-down in the lane. True when a band was hit; it is remembered in
35	    /// `pressed`, and a session starts — with `liveBegin` — ONLY for an action
36	    /// with a length: `duration: 0` is invalid input to the core (the
37	    /// `err_out` channel), not a refusal, so a zero-length band is click to
38	    /// select and nothing else. Nothing is selected here (CI-11).
39	    func pressBand(at point: CGPoint) -> Bool {
40	        guard let hit = bandHit(at: point) else { return false }
41	        pressed = hit.action
42	        hover = nil
43	        guard let clip = clip, let action = clip.actions.first(where: { $0.id == hit.action }),
44	              action.duration > 0
45	        else { return true }
46	        drag = ActionDragSession(
47	            clip: clip, action: action, mode: hit.edge.map { .resize($0) } ?? .move,
48	            grabAt: clipTime(atX: point.x), fps: binding.canvas.fps)
49	        binding.liveBegin()
50	        return true
51	    }
52	
53	    /// Mouse-dragged: one `set_action` per tick; a refused tick is swallowed
54	    /// by `updateLiveEdit`.
55	    func dragBand(to point: CGPoint) {
56	        guard var session = drag else { return }
57	        session.update(clipTime: clipTime(atX: point.x))
58	        drag = session
59	        binding.liveUpdate([session.op])
60	        needsDisplay = true
61	    }
62	
63	    /// Mouse-up: the drag's one undo step, if there was a drag, then the
64	    /// pressed band selected — a click and a drop alike, which parks the
65	    /// playhead at the action's (new) end.
66	    func releaseBand() {
67	        let session = drag
68	        let id = pressed
69	        drag = nil
70	        pressed = nil
71	        if let session { binding.liveEnd(session.undoName) }
72	        if let id { binding.selectAction(id) }
73	        needsDisplay = true
74	    }
75	
76	    // MARK: Hover and cursors
77	
78	    /// One area of the lane's own (only areas it OWNS are removed —
79	    /// app/CLAUDE.md "Tracking areas").
80	    func installLaneTracking() {
81	        for area in trackingAreas where area.owner === self { removeTrackingArea(area) }
82	        addTrackingArea(
83	            NSTrackingArea(
84	                rect: .zero,
85	                options: [.mouseMoved, .mouseEnteredAndExited, .activeInKeyWindow, .inVisibleRect],
86	                owner: self, userInfo: nil))
87	    }
88	
89	    func hoverMoved(with event: NSEvent) {
90	        guard drag == nil else {
91	            hover = nil
92	            return
93	        }
94	        hover = bandHit(at: convert(event.locationInWindow, from: nil))
95	    }
96	
97	    func hoverExited() { hover = nil }
98	
99	    /// `.openHand` over a body, `.resizeLeftRight` over a grip — and nothing
100	    /// over a zero-length band, which a press will not move.
101	    func addBandCursorRects() {
102	        guard let clip = clip else { return }
103	        for band in bandRects() {
104	            guard let action = clip.actions.first(where: { $0.id == band.id }),
105	                  action.duration > 0
106	            else { continue }
107	            addGripCursorRects(band.rect)
108	        }
109	    }
110	
111	    // MARK: Drawing
112	
113	    /// While a drag has moved: the original band as a dashed ghost in the
114	    /// lane, and the HUD where the header row's text was (its buttons stay).
115	    /// The HUD's times are CLIP-relative, the detail row's Start field's.
116	    func drawDragOverlay() {
117	        guard let session = drag, session.didMove, let clip = clip, clip.duration > 0 else {
118	            return
119	        }
120	        let lane = laneRect
121	        let span = CGFloat(clip.duration)
122	        let from = lane.minX + lane.width * CGFloat(session.originalStart) / span
123	        let to = lane.minX + lane.width
124	            * CGFloat(session.originalStart + session.originalDuration) / span
125	        ActionDragSession.drawGhost(
126	            CGRect(x: from, y: lane.minY + 4, width: max(to - from, 2), height: lane.height - 8))
127	        let text = session.hud(base: 0, frames: binding.canvas.timecodeFrames)
128	        ActionDragSession.drawHUD(
129	            text,
130	            at: CGPoint(
131	                x: Self.side, y: Self.top + (Self.headerRow - ActionDragSession.hudHeight) / 2))
132	    }
133	}

3	/// The canvas REGION mode (spec §4.2): drag a rectangle over the picture and
4	/// something is done with it. Two things, so far — `Z` adds a zoom action
5	/// that brings the rectangle to the canvas (`add_zoom_action`, road map 2's
6	/// phase 3b), and the Obscure section's "Place on Canvas" appends the
7	/// rectangle to `video.obscure` (phase 3c).
8	///
9	/// **Why one mode and not two.** Both are the same rectangle in the same
10	/// frame — spec §5.3's Q, source pixels from the centre of the layer's
11	/// cropped rect — dragged with the same gesture over the same picture. A
12	/// second overlay with a second copy of the conversion is exactly the drift
13	/// `CanvasSessions.swift` exists to prevent, so `ZoomRegionSession` carries a
14	/// `CanvasRegionPurpose` and this file branches on it in one place: the
15	/// commit at the bottom.
16	///
17	/// **Why it is not a `PreviewCanvasView` gesture**, and why every piece below
18	/// has the shape it has: `EditorViewController+Eyedropper.swift` argues it in
19	/// full and this file follows it deliberately rather than inventing a second
20	/// shape for a modal canvas mode. The overlay's PRESENCE is the mode (an
21	/// extension can hold no state, and a mode outlives a drag, so it is not a
22	/// canvas session); it is installed through `armCanvasMode`, the one place
23	/// that keeps two modal overlays from stacking; it takes first responder so
24	/// Esc reaches it; it clears its callbacks before it is torn down from inside
25	/// its own event handler; it hands focus back to the canvas overlay on the way
26	/// out; and a `sync…` hook closes it when the selection it was armed for
27	/// moves.
28	///
29	/// **The one thing it does differently.** The eyedropper takes a click and
30	/// this takes a DRAG, so the session lives on the view between mouse-down and
31	/// mouse-up, and the view is given five one-line closures instead of two: two
32	/// coordinate conversions (only `PreviewCanvasView` may map points to canvas
33	/// pixels, spec §11), the resolved frame it draws while dragging, and the two
34	/// outcomes. None of them holds logic; each forwards to a named method here.
35	extension EditorViewController {
36	    /// The armed region mode. Nil is the answer to "is the mode on".
37	    var canvasRegion: CanvasRegionView? {
38	        canvasContainer.subviews.compactMap { $0 as? CanvasRegionView }.first
39	    }
40	
41	    // MARK: - Commands
42	
43	    /// `Z`, and the action lane's Zoom to Region button.
44	    ///
45	    /// It TOGGLES, which the eyedropper had to learn the hard way: once focus
46	    /// has left the overlay — a click in the inspector, a menu — Esc no
47	    /// longer reaches it and the key that armed the mode is the only way back
48	    /// out. Pressing it again while the OTHER purpose is armed switches
49	    /// purpose rather than leaving two half-armed modes to reason about.
50	    @objc func zoomToRegion(_ sender: Any?) { toggleRegionMode(.zoom) }
51	
52	    /// The Obscure section's "Place on Canvas": the same band, appended to
53	    /// `video.obscure` instead of turned into an action.
54	    @objc func placeObscureRegion(_ sender: Any?) { toggleRegionMode(.obscure) }
55	
56	    /// The Actions section's "Zoom Back": the null-region form of the same
57	    /// op, at the playhead. No rectangle to drag, so no mode.
58	    @objc func zoomBack(_ sender: Any?) { zoomBackCommand() }
59	
60	    private func toggleRegionMode(_ purpose: CanvasRegionPurpose) {
61	        if let armed = canvasRegion {
62	            let again = armed.purpose == purpose
63	            endRegionMode()
64	            if again { return }
65	        }
66	        beginRegionMode(purpose)
67	    }
68	
69	    /// Arms the mode over the canvas pane.
70	    ///
71	    /// It refuses rather than putting up a crosshair that could only ever
72	    /// beep — `beginChromaEyedropper`'s rule, and `addActionAtPlayheadCommand`
73	    /// already refuses an action when the playhead is off the clip. There has
74	    /// to be exactly one clip selected (a region belongs to one layer's
75	    /// source pixels; two clips would be two different rectangles), it has to
76	    /// be drawing at the playhead (`regionTarget` asks the canvas, so a
77	    /// clip hidden behind an in/out range or on a locked track says no), and
78	    /// an obscure region needs a free slot.
79	    private func beginRegionMode(_ purpose: CanvasRegionPurpose) {
80	        guard let target = regionTarget(), previewCanvas != nil else {
81	            NSSound.beep()
82	            return
83	        }
84	        if purpose == .obscure, obscureRegions().count >= ObscureProps.max {
85	            NSSound.beep()
86	            return
87	        }
88	        let region = CanvasRegionView(
89	            purpose: purpose, clip: target.id, note: regionNote(purpose, clip: target.id))
90	        // One-line forwards only (app/CLAUDE.md).
91	        region.canvasPoint = { [weak self] point in self?.canvasPixel(atWindow: point) }
92	        region.viewPoint = { [weak self] point in self?.regionViewPoint(point) ?? point }
93	        region.resolvedFrame = { [weak self] session in self?.regionResolvedFrame(session) }
94	        region.onCommit = { [weak self] session in self?.regionCommitted(session) }
95	        region.onCancel = { [weak self] in self?.endRegionMode() }
96	        // The one door in (`EditorViewController+Eyedropper.swift`): it ends an
97	        // armed eyedropper on the way, so the two modes cannot stack.
98	        armCanvasMode(region)
99	    }
100	
101	    /// Disarms it, from Esc, from a second press of the key or the button,
102	    /// from a completed drag, and from `syncRegionMode`.
103	    func endRegionMode() { dismissCanvasMode(canvasRegion) }
104	
105	    /// Called from `refreshCanvas`, beside `syncChromaEyedropper`: the mode is
106	    /// armed for ONE clip, so the moment the selection stops being that clip
107	    /// — or the playhead leaves it, which would put the action's start off the
108	    /// clip — it is aimed at nothing and closes itself.
109	    func syncRegionMode() {
110	        guard let region = canvasRegion else { return }
111	        guard regionTarget()?.id != region.clip else {
112	            // Still aimed at the same clip — but the NOTE is about that
113	            // clip's `during`, not about the moment the mode was armed, and
114	            // Clip ▸ Motion ▸ During, an undo and an agent's `set_video` can
115	            // all add or clear one while the band is up. So it is re-read
116	            // here, where every `refreshCanvas` passes.
117	            region.note = regionNote(region.purpose, clip: region.clip)
118	            return
119	        }
120	        endRegionMode()
121	    }
122	
123	    /// The band's second pill for one clip, or nil: a During motion moves the
124	    /// clip under a zoom solved without it (spec §11, R5-4), and only a zoom
125	    /// is solved.
126	    private func regionNote(_ purpose: CanvasRegionPurpose, clip: UInt32) -> String? {
127	        guard purpose == .zoom else { return nil }
128	        let during = document?.editedProject.snapshot.clip(clip)?.videoProps.motion?.during
129	        return during != nil ? CanvasRegionView.duringNote : nil
130	    }
131	
132	    /// `add_zoom_action` with no region, at the playhead: the clip goes back
133	    /// to its own base `scale`, `x` and `y` over the action's span. The core
134	    /// reads an absent and an explicit null region the same way; the op
135	    /// builder sends the null so a saved call says which it meant.
136	    private func zoomBackCommand() {
137	        guard let document = document, let box = regionTarget(),
138	              let clip = document.editedProject.snapshot.clip(box.id)
139	        else {
140	            NSSound.beep()
141	            return
142	        }
143	        let at = clip.clipTime(document.playhead)
144	        document.applyEdit("Zoom Back", .addZoomAction(clip: clip.id, at: at, region: nil))
145	        selectAddedAction(on: clip.id, at: at, countBefore: clip.actions.count)
146	    }
147	
148	    // MARK: - What the mode is aimed at
149	
150	    /// The one layer a region may be drawn on: the single selected clip, on
151	    /// screen at the playhead and not on a locked track.
152	    ///
153	    /// It is answered as a `CanvasLayerBox` rather than a `ClipSnapshot`
154	    /// because the box IS the question — it exists only for a clip the recipe
155	    /// put on the canvas at this instant, and it carries the EVALUATED
156	    /// transform the rectangle has to be measured through
157	    /// (`CanvasLayerBox.sourcePoint` says why that is the opposite of every
158	    /// other canvas session).
159	    private func regionTarget() -> CanvasLayerBox? {
160	        guard let document = document, document.selection.count == 1,
161	              let id = document.selection.first,
162	              let clip = document.editedProject.snapshot.clip(id), clip.contains(document.playhead),
163	              let box = previewCanvas?.box(for: id), !box.locked
164	        else { return nil }
165	        return box
166	    }
167	
168	    /// The obscure list the mode would append to — the first selected clip
169	    /// with pixels, read through the binding so a playhead inside an action
170	    /// reads that action's end state and not the base props.
171	    private func obscureRegions() -> [ObscureProps] {
172	        inspector?.binding.videoProps.obscure ?? []
173	    }
174	
175	    // MARK: - The overlay's five questions
176	
177	    /// The inverse, landed in the OVERLAY's own coordinates — which are the
178	    /// canvas view's today (the overlay fills the canvas, both are flipped),
179	    /// but the conversion is spelled out rather than assumed.
180	    private func regionViewPoint(_ point: CGPoint) -> CGPoint {
181	        guard let canvas = previewCanvas, let region = canvasRegion else { return point }
182	        return region.convert(canvas.canvasToView(point), from: canvas)
183	    }
184	
185	    /// The rectangle the canvas will actually be showing once this zoom lands,
186	    /// in canvas pixels — what the overlay strokes beside the band so a
187	    /// freely dragged rectangle does not have to be guessed at.
188	    private func regionResolvedFrame(_ session: ZoomRegionSession) -> CGRect? {
189	        guard let box = previewCanvas?.box(for: session.clip),
190	              let source = session.sourceRect(in: box)
191	        else { return nil }
192	        return session.frameRect(in: box, source: source)
193	    }
194	
195	    // MARK: - The commit
196	
197	    /// One finished drag. `mouseUp` is an AppKit event, so both branches
198	    /// commit through the ordinary (non-grouped) door and each is ONE undo
199	    /// step; the eyedropper needs `applyGrouped` only because its answer comes
200	    /// back off a queue.
201	    ///
202	    /// A band too small to mean anything leaves the mode ARMED and beeps —
203	    /// a stray click is a miss, not a decision, which is the rule the
204	    /// eyedropper states for a click that landed off the picture.
205	    private func regionCommitted(_ session: ZoomRegionSession) {
206	        guard let box = previewCanvas?.box(for: session.clip),
207	              let region = session.region(in: box)
208	        else {
209	            NSSound.beep()
210	            return
211	        }
212	        switch session.purpose {
213	        case .zoom:
214	            commitZoom(session, region: region)
215	        case .obscure:
216	            commitObscure(session, region: region)
217	        }
218	    }
219	
220	    /// `add_zoom_action` at the playhead in CLIP time. `fit` unless ⇧ was
221	    /// held, and no `curve`, so the core's `ease_in_out` applies rather than
222	    /// `Curve.default`'s `linear`.
223	    private func commitZoom(_ session: ZoomRegionSession, region: ZoomRegion) {
224	        guard let document = document, let clip = document.editedProject.snapshot.clip(session.clip),
225	              clip.contains(document.playhead)
226	        else {
227	            NSSound.beep()
228	            return
229	        }
230	        endRegionMode()
231	        let at = clip.clipTime(document.playhead)
232	        document.applyEdit(
233	            "Zoom to Region",
234	            .addZoomAction(
235	                clip: clip.id, at: at, region: region, fit: session.fill ? .fill : .fit))
236	        selectAddedAction(on: clip.id, at: at, countBefore: clip.actions.count)
237	    }
238	
239	    /// One more `video.obscure` entry, with the rest of its fields at the
240	    /// defaults the Add button uses.
241	    ///
242	    /// It goes through the INSPECTOR BINDING and not straight to the
243	    /// document, because the binding is the one place that knows an edit made
244	    /// while the playhead sits inside an action belongs to that action's end
245	    /// state (§4.3) — and an animated obscure region is precisely what phase
246	    /// 3c's list-interpolation rule exists for, so bypassing it would break
247	    /// the feature silently.
248	    private func commitObscure(_ session: ZoomRegionSession, region: ZoomRegion) {
249	        guard let inspector = inspector, inspector.binding.ids == [session.clip] else {
250	            // The selection moved out from under the drag.
251	            NSSound.beep()
252	            return
253	        }
254	        let binding = inspector.binding
255	        var next = binding.videoProps.obscure
256	        guard next.count < ObscureProps.max else {
257	            NSSound.beep()
258	            return
259	        }
260	        next.append(
261	            ObscureProps(
262	                x: region.x, y: region.y, width: region.width, height: region.height))
263	        endRegionMode()
264	        binding.apply("Obscure Region", binding.ops(video: VideoPatch(obscure: next)))
265	    }
266	}

268	// MARK: - The overlay
269	
270	/// The mode's view: a transparent sheet over the whole canvas pane that takes
271	/// one drag, draws it, wears the crosshair, and says how to get back out.
272	///
273	/// It holds the purpose, the clip and the live session, and nothing else.
274	/// Where the band landed on the canvas, what the layer under it looks like,
275	/// and what to do about it are all the view controller's — the same division
276	/// `CanvasOverlayView` keeps with `PreviewCanvasView`, and the reason the
277	/// five closures below take and answer plain points and rectangles.
278	final class CanvasRegionView: CanvasModeOverlay {
279	    /// What the band is for. Read here only for the hint pill; the commit
280	    /// branches on the session's copy.
281	    let purpose: CanvasRegionPurpose
282	    /// The clip the mode was armed for.
283	    let clip: UInt32
284	    /// A second hint pill under the first; nil draws none. A `var` because
285	    /// what it says is a fact about the CLIP, which can change while the mode
286	    /// is armed — `syncRegionMode` re-reads it on every `refreshCanvas`.
287	    var note: String? {
288	        didSet {
289	            if note != oldValue { needsDisplay = true }
290	        }
291	    }
292	    /// Live between mouse-down and mouse-up, and nil either side of it.
293	    private(set) var session: ZoomRegionSession?
294	
295	    /// A WINDOW point as canvas pixels; nil when there is no canvas to ask.
296	    var canvasPoint: ((CGPoint) -> CGPoint?)?
297	    /// A canvas point in this view's own coordinates.
298	    var viewPoint: ((CGPoint) -> CGPoint)?
299	    /// The rectangle the zoom will frame, in canvas pixels.
300	    var resolvedFrame: ((ZoomRegionSession) -> CGRect?)?
301	    var onCommit: ((ZoomRegionSession) -> Void)?
302	
303	    private static let zoomHint = "Drag a rectangle to zoom to it · ⇧ fills · Esc to cancel"
304	    private static let obscureHint = "Drag a rectangle to obscure · Esc to cancel"
305	    static let duringNote = "This clip has During motion — the zoom is solved without it"
306	    /// The band's own stroke, and the resolved frame's at a lower alpha —
307	    /// the same ink, because they are two readings of one rectangle.
308	    private static let frameAlpha: CGFloat = 0.45
309	
310	    init(purpose: CanvasRegionPurpose, clip: UInt32, note: String? = nil) {
311	        self.purpose = purpose
312	        self.clip = clip
313	        self.note = note
314	        super.init(frame: .zero)
315	    }
316	
317	    @available(*, unavailable)
318	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
319	        fatalError("CanvasRegionView does not support NSCoder")
320	    }
321	
322	    // MARK: Events
323	
324	    /// The press starts the band wherever it landed — including in the void
325	    /// around the picture. A region's centre is allowed outside the layer
326	    /// (the core asks only that x and y be finite), and dragging in from the
327	    /// margin to catch the edge of the frame is the ordinary way to do it.
328	    override func mouseDown(with event: NSEvent) {
329	        guard let point = canvasPoint?(event.locationInWindow) else {
330	            NSSound.beep()
331	            return
332	        }
333	        session = ZoomRegionSession(
334	            purpose: purpose, clip: clip, anchor: point, current: point,
335	            fill: event.modifierFlags.contains(.shift))
336	        needsDisplay = true
337	    }
338	
339	    override func mouseDragged(with event: NSEvent) {
340	        track(event)
341	    }
342	
343	    /// The release tears this view down from inside this very call — the same
344	    /// shape as the eyedropper's pick — so the last reference to it must not
345	    /// be the superview's.
346	    override func mouseUp(with event: NSEvent) {
347	        track(event)
348	        guard let finished = session else { return }
349	        session = nil
350	        withExtendedLifetime(self) { onCommit?(finished) }
351	    }
352	
353	    /// ⇧ is read at every step rather than latched at the press, so the
354	    /// choice between fit and fill can be made while the band is being drawn
355	    /// and the resolved frame answers it as it is made.
356	    private func track(_ event: NSEvent) {
357	        guard var live = session, let point = canvasPoint?(event.locationInWindow) else { return }
358	        live.update(point: point, fill: event.modifierFlags.contains(.shift))
359	        session = live
360	        needsDisplay = true
361	    }

363	    /// Esc drops a band in progress BEFORE the base runs `onCancel`, so the
364	    /// mode never ends with a live session on it.
365	    override func keyDown(with event: NSEvent) {
366	        if event.keyCode == 53 { session = nil }
367	        super.keyDown(with: event)
368	    }

370	    override func detachCallbacks() {
371	        canvasPoint = nil
372	        viewPoint = nil
373	        resolvedFrame = nil
374	        onCommit = nil
375	        super.detachCallbacks()

380	    override func draw(_ dirtyRect: NSRect) {
381	        drawBand()
382	        drawHint()
383	    }

385	    /// The band, and — for a zoom — the rectangle it resolves to.
386	    ///
387	    /// Both are AXIS-ALIGNED in canvas space (the band by construction, the
388	    /// frame because a zoom changes a layer's scale and position and never
389	    /// its angle), and the canvas-to-view mapping is a scale and a
390	    /// translation, so two converted corners describe each of them. Nothing
391	    /// here is rotated, which is why the marquee's flat rectangle is honest
392	    /// even over a turned clip.
393	    private func drawBand() {
394	        guard let session = session, let convert = viewPoint else { return }
395	        let band = rect(from: convert(session.anchor), to: convert(session.current))
396	        guard band.width >= 1, band.height >= 1 else { return }
397	        let path = NSBezierPath(rect: band.insetBy(dx: 0.5, dy: 0.5))
398	        DS.selectionFill.setFill()
399	        path.fill()
400	        DS.marquee.setStroke()
401	        path.stroke()
402	
403	        guard let canvasFrame = resolvedFrame?(session) else { return }
404	        let frame = rect(
405	            from: convert(CGPoint(x: canvasFrame.minX, y: canvasFrame.minY)),
406	            to: convert(CGPoint(x: canvasFrame.maxX, y: canvasFrame.maxY)))
407	        guard frame.width >= 1, frame.height >= 1 else { return }
408	        let ghost = NSBezierPath(rect: frame.insetBy(dx: 0.5, dy: 0.5))
409	        // Dashed as well as dimmed: the two rectangles coincide on one axis
410	        // under `fit`, and a solid stroke at a lower alpha under a solid one
411	        // reads as a rendering artefact rather than as a second rectangle.
412	        let dash: [CGFloat] = [4, 3]
413	        ghost.setLineDash(dash, count: dash.count, phase: 0)
414	        DS.marquee.withAlphaComponent(Self.frameAlpha).setStroke()
415	        ghost.stroke()
416	    }
417	
418	    private func rect(from a: CGPoint, to b: CGPoint) -> CGRect {
419	        CGRect(
420	            x: min(a.x, b.x), y: min(a.y, b.y), width: abs(b.x - a.x), height: abs(b.y - a.y))
421	    }

424	    /// pills (`drawPill`), so every canvas mode announces itself the same way.

426	        let hint = purpose == .zoom ? Self.zoomHint : Self.obscureHint
427	        let height = drawPill(hint, top: Self.hintTop)
428	        // 6 pt between the two pills: a gap that reads as two lines of one hint.
429	        if let note = note { _ = drawPill(note, top: Self.hintTop + height + 6) }

- With several clips selected, the action goes on the first selected clip under the playhead and is not selected, because only a single selected clip can have a selected action.
- **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** also makes actions: one for Ramp Up and Ramp Down, two for Speed Dip and Speed Burst. They show as bands and edit like any other action. See [Speed](speed.md).

The action is refused when it would overlap another action on the clip or run past the clip's end, so near the end of a clip move the playhead back first, or shorten an existing action.

*Agents:* `add_action` (clip, `at` in clip time, optional `duration`; answers the new id in `new_actions`).

### Zoom to a region

**Zoom to Region** is the screencast zoom: draw a rectangle on the picture, and the clip zooms so that rectangle fills the frame.

1. Select one clip and put the playhead over it.
2. Press **Z**, or click the zoom-in magnifier (Zoom to Region) in the action lane.
3. Drag a rectangle over the canvas. A hint reads "Drag a rectangle to zoom to it · ⇧ fills · Esc to cancel", and a second outline shows exactly what the canvas will show once the zoom lands.
4. Release the mouse.

Frame Job adds a 1-second **Ease In Out** action at the playhead whose end state is the scale and position that bring the rectangle to the canvas. It works through the clip's rotation and crop. The new action is selected.

- **Fit or fill.** By default the whole rectangle is shown (fit). Hold **⇧** while dragging to fill the canvas instead, cropping whatever doesn't match the canvas shape.
- **Scale limit.** The zoom stops at the largest scale a layer can take, and the rectangle stays centred even then.
- **Leaving the mode.** Press Esc, press **Z** again, or click the button again. The mode also closes when the selection changes or the playhead leaves the clip. A rectangle too small to mean anything beeps and leaves the mode on so you can draw again.
- **During motion.** If the clip has a During motion preset, the band shows "This clip has During motion — the zoom is solved without it", because the preset keeps moving the clip under the zoom.

The mode needs exactly one selected clip that is drawn at the playhead and is not on a locked track. Otherwise **Z** beeps.

To zoom a screen recording at every click at once, use **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…**, which plans these same zoom actions from the recording's cursor file (see [Auto Zoom](screen-recording.md#auto-zoom)).

**Zoom Back** (the zoom-out magnifier in the action lane) adds a 1-second **Ease In Out** action at the playhead whose end state is the clip's own base scale, x and y, whatever earlier actions did. Use it after a Zoom to Region to pull back out. It needs the same target as **Z** (one selected clip drawn at the playhead, not on a locked track) and beeps otherwise. The new action is selected.

*Agents:* `add_zoom_action` (`region` as centre and size in source pixels from the centre of the clip's cropped picture, `fit` or `fill`, optional `curve` and `duration`; `region: null` is a zoom back).

### Select an action

An action is selected when you:

- click its band in the timeline or in the Clip tab's action lane,
- add it (with Add Action, Zoom to Region or Zoom Back), or
- play or scrub the playhead **into** its span while its clip is the only one selected.

Clicking a band on a clip that is part of a multi-clip selection selects just that clip and its action.

Clicking a band also moves the playhead to the action's end, so the preview shows the state the Clip tab is editing (one frame short when the action ends with the clip).

Leaving the span keeps the action selected. To leave it, press **Esc**, click the **Clip** chip at the start of the action lane, or select a different clip. Only a single selected clip can have a selected action. Selecting an action is not an undo step and is not saved with the project.

### Edit an action's end state

While an action is selected, every field in the Clip tab shows and sets that action's **end state**, the values the clip reaches at the action's end. The same goes for the canvas: dragging the selected clip's handles, or nudging it with the arrow keys, writes the end state.

Unchecking a switch inside an action (a shadow or an outline, for example) turns that property off when the action ends.

The Clip tab marks each row so you can see what the action touches:

| Mark | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ◆ | This action animates the row. The label turns strong and the field gets a border in the action colour. A popup, checkbox or other on/off control also shows "at end", because it switches rather than ramps |
| ◇ | Another action on the clip animates this row. Its tooltip names the action |
| ○ | The row follows a value this action animates (for example, Gain follows Volume) |
| ⊘ | Actions don't animate this row. Edits change the clip |

A slider on an animated row fills in the action colour from the value at the action's start to the knob. When the playhead is inside the clip, a coral tick shows the value at the playhead. A row that is a field only shows that value as a "now …" tag instead.

Section headers carry the same marks, and a section where every row is ⊘ says "Actions don't animate this. Edits here change the clip." Each sub-tab's label shows **◆N** when the selected action animates N of its keys. When you select an action, the sections it animates on the current sub-tab open automatically.

To take a property back out of an action:

- Hover over a ◆ and click the × that replaces it ("Remove from action N").
- Click **Clear** in a section's header to remove all of that section's keys from the action. While an action is selected and keys the section, Clear takes the place of the header's **Reset**; otherwise Reset shows only while the section differs from its defaults.
- Right-click a row for its menu: **Remove from action N** on an animated row, **Go to action M** on a ◇ row (selects that action), and **Set end value to default** (on a row the selected action animates) or **Reset to default** (otherwise). The default item is disabled when the row already holds its default.

*Agents:* `set_action_end` (a `patch` with `video`, `audio`, `text` and `graphic` groups and a top-level `speed`, merged into the end state; `null` removes a key; `off` lists `"group.key"` paths to switch off at the end). `video.motion` and `text.words` are refused.

### Move, resize and re-curve an action

**In the action lane or the timeline:**

- Drag a band's **body** to move the action within its clip.
- Drag a band's outer 5 pt (its grips, shown on hover) to move that end. A band 15 pt wide or narrower has no grips and only moves.

A drag snaps to whole frames, keeps the action at least one frame long, and stops at the neighbouring actions and the clip's ends. A dashed outline marks where the band started. A readout replaces the lane's header text: "start → end +s:ff" for a move or a start resize, "len +Nf" for an end resize. The whole drag is one undo step (**Move Action** or **Resize Action**). Dropping the band selects the action. Bands don't snap to the playhead or other edits. If Frame Job would refuse a position, the band just stops there.

**In the action lane's detail row** (shown while an action is selected):

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| Start | Where the action starts, as a timecode measured from the clip's start |
| Length | How long it takes, 0.01–36000 s (quick picks 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2) |
| Curve | Linear, In, Out or In Out, with a glyph of the curve beside it |
| Trash button | Removes the action |

When Frame Job refuses a typed Start or Length, or an end-state edit, the reason appears at the foot of the inspector as "Refused: …" with the rule's own sentence. It stays until the project next changes or you click it. A band drag never shows one.

*Agents:* `set_action` (`start`, `duration`, `curve`; any left out keep their value).

### Remove an action

With an action selected, press **⌫**, or click the trash button in the action lane. ⌫ removes only the action, not the clip.

Careful: **⌘⌫** (Ripple Delete) still ripple-deletes the whole selected clip, even while an action is selected.

A speed action can't be removed if doing so would make the clip read past the end of its media. The refusal names the latest clip end that fits. See [Speed](speed.md).

*Agents:* `remove_action`.

### Actions on the timeline

Each clip that has an action shows an **action lane** directly under its name strip, with one band per action. How much a band shows depends on **View ▸ Timeline Track Height**:

| Track height | A band shows |
|---|---|
| Small | The bar only |
| Medium | Its number, a zoom glyph for a zoom action, and the curve on the selected band |
| Large | All of that, plus the properties it changes (for example `scale, x, y`, or `speed`) |

Actions are numbered in time order, and the number is the same on the timeline and in the Clip tab. The selected action's band is solid, a wash runs down the clip under its span, and the span is shaded on the ruler.

### The action lane in the Clip tab

The Clip tab opens with a pinned block above its sections: the selection header, the action lane, and the sub-tabs. The action lane is a small timeline of the selected clip:

- **Header row:** ACTIONS, then the count (or "none") and "· editing N" while action N is selected, then three buttons: Zoom to Region (Z), Zoom Back, and Add Action (⌥⌘K).
- **Lane row:** the **Clip** chip (highlighted while no action is selected; click it to leave the action), then the whole clip with its actions as numbered bands and the playhead. Under the bands the lane also shows the clip's transition overlap (hatched), its audio fades and its motion wedges, the same marks the timeline draws. An empty lane reads "no actions · ⌥⌘K adds one".
- **Detail row:** only while an action is selected (see above).

With several clips selected the lane reads "Select one clip to edit its actions."

### How edits move actions

| Edit | What happens to the clip's actions |
|---|---|
| Trim the start | Actions keep their clip time, so they stay put relative to the clip's new start |
| Trim the end | Actions stay put, so one can end up running past the clip's new end; only the part inside the clip plays. You can still move it earlier, shorten it or change its curve, but not make it end any later |
| Slip or Roll | Actions stay where they are in clip time |
| Change the speed, or rate-stretch | Actions keep their place as a fraction of the clip |
| Split | Actions after the cut go to the second half; one that spans the cut is divided between the halves |
| Add a transition at a hard cut | The incoming clip's actions move with its new first frame, so a zoom stays on the frame it was drawn over |
| Duplicate, Copy and Paste | The copies keep their actions |
| Nest | The clips keep their actions inside the nest |
| Detach Audio | The new audio clip gets a copy of every action, so volume actions keep working |
| Freeze Frame | The still has no actions; the look at the frozen frame is baked into its own properties |
| Add Blurred Background | The backdrop copy has no actions, so a zoom on the foreground doesn't zoom the backdrop |
| Paste Attributes | Actions are not copied |

### On the timeline

A clip with an In or Out preset shows a small wedge along the bottom of its name strip, as long as the preset's duration at the current zoom. If the wedges overlap, the two presets are longer than the clip together. In that case Frame Job shortens both in proportion to their lengths, so the entrance ends on the frame where the exit begins, rather than refusing.

A clip with a During movement shows a small wave symbol at the right end of its name strip.

### Inactive presets

An In or Out with a zero duration can come from an agent or an older project. It is kept but does nothing. The section, the summary and the Motion menu mark it "(inactive)" (or "(some inactive)" across a selection), it draws no wedge, and a note reads "Selection includes inactive In motion (zero duration). Increase Duration to reactivate; choose None to clear."

### Limits

- A preset is not part of any action. Motion rows are ⊘, and edits always write the clip, even with an action selected.
- A split gives the first half no Out and the second half no In, so the cut doesn't play an exit and an entrance. A During movement restarts at each cut, so Remove Silences on a clip with Pulse or Drift can make it jump at the cuts.
- Freeze frame and Add Blurred Background drop the motion. Duplicate, Detach Audio and Paste keep it. Changing the speed doesn't rescale the presets.
- A text clip has no measured size, so a slide starts or ends half a canvas past the edge. That clears any text narrower than the canvas.
- A canvas drag started mid-motion starts from the clip's un-moved position.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**

  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`

  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`

  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and

  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and

  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept

  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil

  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.

  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.

  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`

  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.

  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-66);

  core's `none`: a case named `none` warns), `CursorProps` (`VideoProps.cursor` and
  `VideoPatch.cursor`; its `dictionary` writes all eight keys, `NSNull` for a nil `hideIdle`),
  `CursorPatch` (all eight keys, the sparse write `VideoPatch.cursorPart` carries — written
  under `cursor` only when `cursor` is nil, never decoded, `cutoutPart`'s shape — so each Cursor
  row writes its own key alone, CU3b, CU4, spec §11 CU-38 (b), CU-40; `clipsOwn` (smoothing,
  hide_idle) and `animatable` (the other six)), with `CursorProps.smoothingSteps`,

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

3	/// The selected clip's actions as a mini timeline (spec §11 CI-1, CI-4):
4	/// a header row (ACTIONS, the count, "· editing N", and Zoom to Region, Zoom
5	/// Back and Add Action), a lane row (the Clip chip, then the whole clip with
6	/// its bands by fraction, numbered in time order, and the playhead), and —
7	/// only while an action is selected — a detail row: Start (clip-relative),
8	/// Length, Curve and Remove, each an ordinary `set_action` / `remove_action`.
9	///
10	/// Built once per pane build; the pane rebuilds whenever the selected clip or
11	/// the selected action changes (the default `structureSignature` keys on
12	/// `InspectorBinding.action(_:)`), so the ids captured here are the ones on
13	/// screen, and every read goes fresh through them.
14	///
15	/// A band is dragged here as on the timeline (spec §11 CI-11,
16	/// `ActionLaneView+Drag.swift`), and the well carries the clip's hatch, fades
17	/// and wedges under the bands (CI-12, `ActionLaneDecor.swift`).

41	    /// them only when this changes, never on a playhead-only refresh.

44

47	        self.inspector = inspector
48	        let single = binding.isSingle ? binding.primary?.id : nil
49	        clipID = single

102	    /// and bottom, at least 2 pt wide.
103	    func bandRects() -> [(id: UInt32, rect: CGRect)] {

3	/// The timeline's half of the selected action (spec §11 CI-1, CI-4): each
4	/// clip's ACTION LANE directly under its name strip, the band hit, the
5	/// selected span's wash down the clip body, and its shade on the ruler.
6	///
7	/// Extensions rather than lines in `TimelineView.swift`, which is frozen at
8	/// wiring (app/CLAUDE.md): the frozen file keeps one call in `hit(at:)`, one
9	/// in the ruler's `draw`, and `TimelineClipDrawing.swift` the two calls in a
10	/// clip's paint order — the wash before the name strip, the bands after it.
11	extension TimelineContentView {
12	    /// The lane: the top of the clip's content rect (under the name strip),
13	    /// full clip width, `DS.actionLaneHeights` tall at S/M/L — never taller
14	    /// than the content it sits in.
15	    static func actionLane(content: CGRect, sizeIndex: Int) -> CGRect {
16	        let heights = DS.actionLaneHeights
17	        let height = heights[min(max(sizeIndex, 0), heights.count - 1)]
18	        return CGRect(
19	            x: content.minX, y: content.minY, width: content.width,
20	            height: min(height, content.height))
21	    }

23	    /// One action's band in the lane: its span, by CLIP time mapped back
24	    /// through the clip's own start, at least 2 pt wide.
25	    static func bandRect(
26	        _ a: ActionSnapshot, clip: ClipSnapshot, lane: CGRect, layout: TimelineLayout
27	    ) -> CGRect {
28	        let from = layout.x(for: clip.start + a.start)
29	        let to = layout.x(for: clip.start + a.endTime)
30	        return CGRect(x: from, y: lane.minY, width: max(to - from, 2), height: lane.height)

33	    /// The action whose band holds `point` — the LANE only, so a press on the
34	    /// clip body below it is still the clip. `hit(at:)` asks after the fade
35	    /// handles, which on an audio-only clip sit inside this lane and are
36	    /// painted over it, and before the edge grabs. Where bands overlap (the
37	    /// 2 pt minimum width, or a hand-written project) the LAST holding the
38	    /// point in `ActionBands.ordered` order wins, because bands paint in that
39	    /// order and it is the one on top — the Clip tab lane's `bandHit` rule. A
40	    /// zero-length band is never painted here, so unlike the lane it is never
41	    /// hit.
42	    func actionBandHit(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, rect: CGRect, at point: CGPoint) -> UInt32? {
43	        guard let owner = timeline else { return nil }
44	        let lane = Self.actionLane(
45	            content: Self.contentRect(rect), sizeIndex: owner.trackHeightIndex)
46	        guard lane.height > 0, lane.contains(point) else { return nil }
47	        return ActionBands.ordered(clip).last { action in
48	            action.duration > 0
49	                && Self.bandRect(action, clip: clip, lane: lane, layout: owner.layout)
50	                    .contains(point)
51	        }?.id
52	    }

54	    /// What a press at `point` grabs on the clip's action lane: a band's grip
55	    /// (`.actionEdge`) or its body (`.action`), or nil off every band. The
56	    /// band is `actionBandHit`'s, unchanged; the grip is asked of that band's
57	    /// own rect (spec §11 CI-11).
58	    func actionHit(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, rect: CGRect, at point: CGPoint) -> TimelineHit? {
59	        guard let owner = timeline, let id = actionBandHit(clip, rect: rect, at: point),
60	              let action = clip.actions.first(where: { $0.id == id })
61	        else { return nil }
62	        let lane = Self.actionLane(
63	            content: Self.contentRect(rect), sizeIndex: owner.trackHeightIndex)
64	        let band = Self.bandRect(action, clip: clip, lane: lane, layout: owner.layout)
65	        if let edge = ActionBands.gripEdge(in: band, at: point.x) {
66	            return .actionEdge(clip: clip.id, action: id, edge)
67	        }
68	        return .action(clip: clip.id, action: id)
69	    }

71	    /// The selected span down the whole clip body: the action ink at 12 %
72	    /// with 1 pt ends at 55 %. Drawn before the name strip, so the strip
73	    /// still reads over it.

76	              let action = clip.actions.first(where: { $0.id == id })

80	        let to = layout.x(for: clip.start + action.endTime)
81	        let span = CGRect(x: from, y: body.minY, width: max(to - from, 2), height: body.height)
82	        DS.action.withAlphaComponent(0.12).setFill()
83	        span.fill()
84	        DS.action.withAlphaComponent(0.55).setFill()
85	        NSRect(x: span.minX, y: span.minY, width: 1, height: span.height).fill()
86	        NSRect(x: span.maxX - 1, y: span.minY, width: 1, height: span.height).fill()
87	    }

89	    /// The lane's black-22 % backing and every band on it, numbered in time
90	    /// order, then — from M, on a clip whose rate moves — the rate line over
91	    /// them, inset 2 pt top and bottom (spec §11 SR-26). The backing is drawn
92	    /// only on a clip that has an action with a length (road map 9 §2's
93	    /// deviation: the handoff draws it on every clip).
94	    func drawActionBands(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, rect: CGRect, owner: TimelineView) {
95	        guard clip.actions.contains(where: { $0.duration > 0 }) else { return }
96	        let lane = Self.actionLane(
97	            content: Self.contentRect(rect), sizeIndex: owner.trackHeightIndex)
98	        guard lane.height > 0 else { return }
99	        NSColor.black.withAlphaComponent(0.22).setFill()
100	        lane.fill()
101	        let level = ActionBands.Level(sizeIndex: owner.trackHeightIndex)
102	        let graph = level == .bars ? nil : RateGraph.points(
103	            owner.sourceMaps(clip.id), in: lane.insetBy(dx: 0, dy: 2),
104	            x: { owner.layout.x(for: clip.start + $0) })
105	        for (index, action) in ActionBands.ordered(clip).enumerated() where action.duration > 0 {
106	            ActionBands.draw(
107	                band: Self.bandRect(action, clip: clip, lane: lane, layout: owner.layout),
108	                number: index + 1,
109	                label: ActionBands.keys(of: action.end).joined(separator: ", "),
110	                curve: RateGraph.bandCurve(action, graphed: graph != nil),
111	                zoom: ActionBands.isZoom(action),
112	                selected: owner.selectedAction == action.id,
113	                hovered: owner.bandHover?.clip == clip.id && owner.bandHover?.action == action.id,
114	                level: level)
115	        }
116	        if let graph { RateGraph.draw(graph, in: lane) }
117	    }
118	}

3	/// Retiming an action by dragging its band in the Clip tab's lane (spec §11
4	/// CI-11) — the same `ActionDragSession` the timeline drags with, through the
5	/// binding's live trio, so a drag is ONE undo step.
6	///
7	/// The lane selects at mouse-UP, not at the press as the timeline does: a
8	/// selection rebuilds the pane, and the pane must not rebuild under the
9	/// pointer (`refresh(isLive:)` skips rebuilds only while a live edit runs).
10	/// A click and a drop therefore share one path, `releaseBand`.
11	extension ActionLaneView {
12	    /// The clip time under `x`: the lane's fraction of the clip's length,
13	    /// clamped to the clip.
14	    func clipTime(atX x: CGFloat) -> Ticks {
15	        guard let clip = clip, clip.duration > 0 else { return 0 }
16	        let lane = laneRect
17	        guard lane.width > 0 else { return 0 }
18	        let fraction = min(max((x - lane.minX) / lane.width, 0), 1)
19	        return Ticks((Double(fraction) * Double(clip.duration)).rounded())
20	    }
21	
22	    /// The band under `point` and the grip it is in, if any. The LAST band
23	    /// holding the point wins, because bands paint in time order and that is
24	    /// the one on top — so a zero-length band sitting on another's start is
25	    /// the one a press takes. A zero-length band answers too (it is
26	    /// selectable), always with no edge: 2 pt is all body.
27	    func bandHit(at point: CGPoint) -> ActionBandHover? {
28	        guard let clipID, let band = bandRects().last(where: { $0.rect.contains(point) })
29	        else { return nil }
30	        return ActionBandHover(
31	            clip: clipID, action: band.id, edge: ActionBands.gripEdge(in: band.rect, at: point.x))
32	    }
33	
34	    /// Mouse-down in the lane. True when a band was hit; it is remembered in
35	    /// `pressed`, and a session starts — with `liveBegin` — ONLY for an action
36	    /// with a length: `duration: 0` is invalid input to the core (the
37	    /// `err_out` channel), not a refusal, so a zero-length band is click to
38	    /// select and nothing else. Nothing is selected here (CI-11).
39	    func pressBand(at point: CGPoint) -> Bool {
40	        guard let hit = bandHit(at: point) else { return false }
41	        pressed = hit.action
42	        hover = nil
43	        guard let clip = clip, let action = clip.actions.first(where: { $0.id == hit.action }),
44	              action.duration > 0
45	        else { return true }
46	        drag = ActionDragSession(
47	            clip: clip, action: action, mode: hit.edge.map { .resize($0) } ?? .move,
48	            grabAt: clipTime(atX: point.x), fps: binding.canvas.fps)
49	        binding.liveBegin()
50	        return true
51	    }
52	
53	    /// Mouse-dragged: one `set_action` per tick; a refused tick is swallowed
54	    /// by `updateLiveEdit`.
55	    func dragBand(to point: CGPoint) {
56	        guard var session = drag else { return }
57	        session.update(clipTime: clipTime(atX: point.x))
58	        drag = session
59	        binding.liveUpdate([session.op])
60	        needsDisplay = true
61	    }
62	
63	    /// Mouse-up: the drag's one undo step, if there was a drag, then the
64	    /// pressed band selected — a click and a drop alike, which parks the
65	    /// playhead at the action's (new) end.
66	    func releaseBand() {
67	        let session = drag
68	        let id = pressed
69	        drag = nil
70	        pressed = nil
71	        if let session { binding.liveEnd(session.undoName) }
72	        if let id { binding.selectAction(id) }
73	        needsDisplay = true
74	    }
75	
76	    // MARK: Hover and cursors
77	
78	    /// One area of the lane's own (only areas it OWNS are removed —
79	    /// app/CLAUDE.md "Tracking areas").
80	    func installLaneTracking() {
81	        for area in trackingAreas where area.owner === self { removeTrackingArea(area) }
82	        addTrackingArea(
83	            NSTrackingArea(
84	                rect: .zero,
85	                options: [.mouseMoved, .mouseEnteredAndExited, .activeInKeyWindow, .inVisibleRect],
86	                owner: self, userInfo: nil))
87	    }
88	
89	    func hoverMoved(with event: NSEvent) {
90	        guard drag == nil else {
91	            hover = nil
92	            return
93	        }
94	        hover = bandHit(at: convert(event.locationInWindow, from: nil))
95	    }
96	
97	    func hoverExited() { hover = nil }
98	
99	    /// `.openHand` over a body, `.resizeLeftRight` over a grip — and nothing
100	    /// over a zero-length band, which a press will not move.
101	    func addBandCursorRects() {
102	        guard let clip = clip else { return }
103	        for band in bandRects() {
104	            guard let action = clip.actions.first(where: { $0.id == band.id }),
105	                  action.duration > 0
106	            else { continue }
107	            addGripCursorRects(band.rect)
108	        }
109	    }
110	
111	    // MARK: Drawing
112	
113	    /// While a drag has moved: the original band as a dashed ghost in the
114	    /// lane, and the HUD where the header row's text was (its buttons stay).
115	    /// The HUD's times are CLIP-relative, the detail row's Start field's.
116	    func drawDragOverlay() {
117	        guard let session = drag, session.didMove, let clip = clip, clip.duration > 0 else {
118	            return
119	        }
120	        let lane = laneRect
121	        let span = CGFloat(clip.duration)
122	        let from = lane.minX + lane.width * CGFloat(session.originalStart) / span
123	        let to = lane.minX + lane.width
124	            * CGFloat(session.originalStart + session.originalDuration) / span
125	        ActionDragSession.drawGhost(
126	            CGRect(x: from, y: lane.minY + 4, width: max(to - from, 2), height: lane.height - 8))
127	        let text = session.hud(base: 0, frames: binding.canvas.timecodeFrames)
128	        ActionDragSession.drawHUD(
129	            text,
130	            at: CGPoint(
131	                x: Self.side, y: Self.top + (Self.headerRow - ActionDragSession.hudHeight) / 2))
132	    }
133	}

3	/// The canvas REGION mode (spec §4.2): drag a rectangle over the picture and
4	/// something is done with it. Two things, so far — `Z` adds a zoom action
5	/// that brings the rectangle to the canvas (`add_zoom_action`, road map 2's
6	/// phase 3b), and the Obscure section's "Place on Canvas" appends the
7	/// rectangle to `video.obscure` (phase 3c).
8	///
9	/// **Why one mode and not two.** Both are the same rectangle in the same
10	/// frame — spec §5.3's Q, source pixels from the centre of the layer's
11	/// cropped rect — dragged with the same gesture over the same picture. A
12	/// second overlay with a second copy of the conversion is exactly the drift
13	/// `CanvasSessions.swift` exists to prevent, so `ZoomRegionSession` carries a
14	/// `CanvasRegionPurpose` and this file branches on it in one place: the
15	/// commit at the bottom.
16	///
17	/// **Why it is not a `PreviewCanvasView` gesture**, and why every piece below
18	/// has the shape it has: `EditorViewController+Eyedropper.swift` argues it in
19	/// full and this file follows it deliberately rather than inventing a second
20	/// shape for a modal canvas mode. The overlay's PRESENCE is the mode (an
21	/// extension can hold no state, and a mode outlives a drag, so it is not a
22	/// canvas session); it is installed through `armCanvasMode`, the one place
23	/// that keeps two modal overlays from stacking; it takes first responder so
24	/// Esc reaches it; it clears its callbacks before it is torn down from inside
25	/// its own event handler; it hands focus back to the canvas overlay on the way
26	/// out; and a `sync…` hook closes it when the selection it was armed for
27	/// moves.
28	///
29	/// **The one thing it does differently.** The eyedropper takes a click and
30	/// this takes a DRAG, so the session lives on the view between mouse-down and
31	/// mouse-up, and the view is given five one-line closures instead of two: two
32	/// coordinate conversions (only `PreviewCanvasView` may map points to canvas
33	/// pixels, spec §11), the resolved frame it draws while dragging, and the two
34	/// outcomes. None of them holds logic; each forwards to a named method here.
35	extension EditorViewController {
36	    /// The armed region mode. Nil is the answer to "is the mode on".
37	    var canvasRegion: CanvasRegionView? {
38	        canvasContainer.subviews.compactMap { $0 as? CanvasRegionView }.first
39	    }
40	
41	    // MARK: - Commands
42	
43	    /// `Z`, and the action lane's Zoom to Region button.
44	    ///
45	    /// It TOGGLES, which the eyedropper had to learn the hard way: once focus
46	    /// has left the overlay — a click in the inspector, a menu — Esc no
47	    /// longer reaches it and the key that armed the mode is the only way back
48	    /// out. Pressing it again while the OTHER purpose is armed switches
49	    /// purpose rather than leaving two half-armed modes to reason about.
50	    @objc func zoomToRegion(_ sender: Any?) { toggleRegionMode(.zoom) }
51	
52	    /// The Obscure section's "Place on Canvas": the same band, appended to
53	    /// `video.obscure` instead of turned into an action.
54	    @objc func placeObscureRegion(_ sender: Any?) { toggleRegionMode(.obscure) }
55	
56	    /// The Actions section's "Zoom Back": the null-region form of the same
57	    /// op, at the playhead. No rectangle to drag, so no mode.
58	    @objc func zoomBack(_ sender: Any?) { zoomBackCommand() }
59	
60	    private func toggleRegionMode(_ purpose: CanvasRegionPurpose) {
61	        if let armed = canvasRegion {
62	            let again = armed.purpose == purpose
63	            endRegionMode()
64	            if again { return }
65	        }
66	        beginRegionMode(purpose)
67	    }
68	
69	    /// Arms the mode over the canvas pane.
70	    ///
71	    /// It refuses rather than putting up a crosshair that could only ever
72	    /// beep — `beginChromaEyedropper`'s rule, and `addActionAtPlayheadCommand`
73	    /// already refuses an action when the playhead is off the clip. There has
74	    /// to be exactly one clip selected (a region belongs to one layer's
75	    /// source pixels; two clips would be two different rectangles), it has to
76	    /// be drawing at the playhead (`regionTarget` asks the canvas, so a
77	    /// clip hidden behind an in/out range or on a locked track says no), and
78	    /// an obscure region needs a free slot.
79	    private func beginRegionMode(_ purpose: CanvasRegionPurpose) {
80	        guard let target = regionTarget(), previewCanvas != nil else {
81	            NSSound.beep()
82	            return
83	        }
84	        if purpose == .obscure, obscureRegions().count >= ObscureProps.max {
85	            NSSound.beep()
86	            return
87	        }
88	        let region = CanvasRegionView(
89	            purpose: purpose, clip: target.id, note: regionNote(purpose, clip: target.id))
90	        // One-line forwards only (app/CLAUDE.md).
91	        region.canvasPoint = { [weak self] point in self?.canvasPixel(atWindow: point) }
92	        region.viewPoint = { [weak self] point in self?.regionViewPoint(point) ?? point }
93	        region.resolvedFrame = { [weak self] session in self?.regionResolvedFrame(session) }
94	        region.onCommit = { [weak self] session in self?.regionCommitted(session) }
95	        region.onCancel = { [weak self] in self?.endRegionMode() }
96	        // The one door in (`EditorViewController+Eyedropper.swift`): it ends an
97	        // armed eyedropper on the way, so the two modes cannot stack.
98	        armCanvasMode(region)
99	    }
100	
101	    /// Disarms it, from Esc, from a second press of the key or the button,
102	    /// from a completed drag, and from `syncRegionMode`.
103	    func endRegionMode() { dismissCanvasMode(canvasRegion) }
104	
105	    /// Called from `refreshCanvas`, beside `syncChromaEyedropper`: the mode is
106	    /// armed for ONE clip, so the moment the selection stops being that clip
107	    /// — or the playhead leaves it, which would put the action's start off the
108	    /// clip — it is aimed at nothing and closes itself.
109	    func syncRegionMode() {
110	        guard let region = canvasRegion else { return }
111	        guard regionTarget()?.id != region.clip else {
112	            // Still aimed at the same clip — but the NOTE is about that
113	            // clip's `during`, not about the moment the mode was armed, and
114	            // Clip ▸ Motion ▸ During, an undo and an agent's `set_video` can
115	            // all add or clear one while the band is up. So it is re-read
116	            // here, where every `refreshCanvas` passes.
117	            region.note = regionNote(region.purpose, clip: region.clip)
118	            return
119	        }
120	        endRegionMode()
121	    }

123	    /// The band's second pill for one clip, or nil: a During motion moves the
124	    /// clip under a zoom solved without it (spec §11, R5-4), and only a zoom
125	    /// is solved.
126	    private func regionNote(_ purpose: CanvasRegionPurpose, clip: UInt32) -> String? {
127	        guard purpose == .zoom else { return nil }
128	        let during = document?.editedProject.snapshot.clip(clip)?.videoProps.motion?.during
129	        return during != nil ? CanvasRegionView.duringNote : nil
130	    }

132	    /// `add_zoom_action` with no region, at the playhead: the clip goes back
133	    /// to its own base `scale`, `x` and `y` over the action's span. The core
134	    /// reads an absent and an explicit null region the same way; the op
135	    /// builder sends the null so a saved call says which it meant.
136	    private func zoomBackCommand() {
137	        guard let document = document, let box = regionTarget(),
138	              let clip = document.editedProject.snapshot.clip(box.id)
139	        else {
140	            NSSound.beep()
141	            return
142	        }
143	        let at = clip.clipTime(document.playhead)
144	        document.applyEdit("Zoom Back", .addZoomAction(clip: clip.id, at: at, region: nil))
145	        selectAddedAction(on: clip.id, at: at, countBefore: clip.actions.count)
146	    }
147	
148	    // MARK: - What the mode is aimed at
149	
150	    /// The one layer a region may be drawn on: the single selected clip, on
151	    /// screen at the playhead and not on a locked track.
152	    ///
153	    /// It is answered as a `CanvasLayerBox` rather than a `ClipSnapshot`
154	    /// because the box IS the question — it exists only for a clip the recipe
155	    /// put on the canvas at this instant, and it carries the EVALUATED
156	    /// transform the rectangle has to be measured through
157	    /// (`CanvasLayerBox.sourcePoint` says why that is the opposite of every
158	    /// other canvas session).
159	    private func regionTarget() -> CanvasLayerBox? {
160	        guard let document = document, document.selection.count == 1,
161	              let id = document.selection.first,
162	              let clip = document.editedProject.snapshot.clip(id), clip.contains(document.playhead),
163	              let box = previewCanvas?.box(for: id), !box.locked
164	        else { return nil }
165	        return box
166	    }
