168	    /// The obscure list the mode would append to — the first selected clip
169	    /// with pixels, read through the binding so a playhead inside an action
170	    /// reads that action's end state and not the base props.
171	    private func obscureRegions() -> [ObscureProps] {
172	        inspector?.binding.videoProps.obscure ?? []
173	    }

175	    // MARK: - The overlay's five questions
176	
177	    /// The inverse, landed in the OVERLAY's own coordinates — which are the
178	    /// canvas view's today (the overlay fills the canvas, both are flipped),
179	    /// but the conversion is spelled out rather than assumed.
180	    private func regionViewPoint(_ point: CGPoint) -> CGPoint {
181	        guard let canvas = previewCanvas, let region = canvasRegion else { return point }
182	        return region.convert(canvas.canvasToView(point), from: canvas)
183	    }

185	    /// The rectangle the canvas will actually be showing once this zoom lands,
186	    /// in canvas pixels — what the overlay strokes beside the band so a
187	    /// freely dragged rectangle does not have to be guessed at.
188	    private func regionResolvedFrame(_ session: ZoomRegionSession) -> CGRect? {
189	        guard let box = previewCanvas?.box(for: session.clip),
190	              let source = session.sourceRect(in: box)
191	        else { return nil }
192	        return session.frameRect(in: box, source: source)
193	    }

195	    // MARK: - The commit
196	
197	    /// One finished drag. `mouseUp` is an AppKit event, so both branches
198	    /// commit through the ordinary (non-grouped) door and each is ONE undo
199	    /// step; the eyedropper needs `applyGrouped` only because its answer comes
200	    /// back off a queue.
201	    ///
202	    /// A band too small to mean anything leaves the mode ARMED and beeps —
203	    /// a stray click is a miss, not a decision, which is the rule the
204	    /// eyedropper states for a click that landed off the picture.
205	    private func regionCommitted(_ session: ZoomRegionSession) {
206	        guard let box = previewCanvas?.box(for: session.clip),
207	              let region = session.region(in: box)
208	        else {
209	            NSSound.beep()
210	            return
211	        }
212	        switch session.purpose {
213	        case .zoom:
214	            commitZoom(session, region: region)
215	        case .obscure:
216	            commitObscure(session, region: region)
217	        }
218	    }

220	    /// `add_zoom_action` at the playhead in CLIP time. `fit` unless ⇧ was
221	    /// held, and no `curve`, so the core's `ease_in_out` applies rather than
222	    /// `Curve.default`'s `linear`.
223	    private func commitZoom(_ session: ZoomRegionSession, region: ZoomRegion) {
224	        guard let document = document, let clip = document.editedProject.snapshot.clip(session.clip),
225	              clip.contains(document.playhead)
226	        else {
227	            NSSound.beep()
228	            return
229	        }
230	        endRegionMode()
231	        let at = clip.clipTime(document.playhead)
232	        document.applyEdit(
233	            "Zoom to Region",
234	            .addZoomAction(
235	                clip: clip.id, at: at, region: region, fit: session.fill ? .fill : .fit))
236	        selectAddedAction(on: clip.id, at: at, countBefore: clip.actions.count)
237	    }

- With several clips selected, the action goes on the first selected clip under the playhead and is not selected, because only a single selected clip can have a selected action.
- **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** also makes actions: one for Ramp Up and Ramp Down, two for Speed Dip and Speed Burst. They show as bands and edit like any other action. See [Speed](speed.md).

The action is refused when it would overlap another action on the clip or run past the clip's end, so near the end of a clip move the playhead back first, or shorten an existing action.

*Agents:* `add_action` (clip, `at` in clip time, optional `duration`; answers the new id in `new_actions`).

### Zoom to a region

**Zoom to Region** is the screencast zoom: draw a rectangle on the picture, and the clip zooms so that rectangle fills the frame.

1. Select one clip and put the playhead over it.
2. Press **Z**, or click the zoom-in magnifier (Zoom to Region) in the action lane.
3. Drag a rectangle over the canvas. A hint reads "Drag a rectangle to zoom to it · ⇧ fills · Esc to cancel", and a second outline shows exactly what the canvas will show once the zoom lands.
4. Release the mouse.

Frame Job adds a 1-second **Ease In Out** action at the playhead whose end state is the scale and position that bring the rectangle to the canvas. It works through the clip's rotation and crop. The new action is selected.

- **Fit or fill.** By default the whole rectangle is shown (fit). Hold **⇧** while dragging to fill the canvas instead, cropping whatever doesn't match the canvas shape.
- **Scale limit.** The zoom stops at the largest scale a layer can take, and the rectangle stays centred even then.
- **Leaving the mode.** Press Esc, press **Z** again, or click the button again. The mode also closes when the selection changes or the playhead leaves the clip. A rectangle too small to mean anything beeps and leaves the mode on so you can draw again.
- **During motion.** If the clip has a During motion preset, the band shows "This clip has During motion — the zoom is solved without it", because the preset keeps moving the clip under the zoom.

The mode needs exactly one selected clip that is drawn at the playhead and is not on a locked track. Otherwise **Z** beeps.

To zoom a screen recording at every click at once, use **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…**, which plans these same zoom actions from the recording's cursor file (see [Auto Zoom](screen-recording.md#auto-zoom)).

**Zoom Back** (the zoom-out magnifier in the action lane) adds a 1-second **Ease In Out** action at the playhead whose end state is the clip's own base scale, x and y, whatever earlier actions did. Use it after a Zoom to Region to pull back out. It needs the same target as **Z** (one selected clip drawn at the playhead, not on a locked track) and beeps otherwise. The new action is selected.

*Agents:* `add_zoom_action` (`region` as centre and size in source pixels from the centre of the clip's cropped picture, `fit` or `fill`, optional `curve` and `duration`; `region: null` is a zoom back).

### Select an action

An action is selected when you:

- click its band in the timeline or in the Clip tab's action lane,
- add it (with Add Action, Zoom to Region or Zoom Back), or
- play or scrub the playhead **into** its span while its clip is the only one selected.

Clicking a band on a clip that is part of a multi-clip selection selects just that clip and its action.

Clicking a band also moves the playhead to the action's end, so the preview shows the state the Clip tab is editing (one frame short when the action ends with the clip).

Leaving the span keeps the action selected. To leave it, press **Esc**, click the **Clip** chip at the start of the action lane, or select a different clip. Only a single selected clip can have a selected action. Selecting an action is not an undo step and is not saved with the project.

### Edit an action's end state

While an action is selected, every field in the Clip tab shows and sets that action's **end state**, the values the clip reaches at the action's end. The same goes for the canvas: dragging the selected clip's handles, or nudging it with the arrow keys, writes the end state.

Unchecking a switch inside an action (a shadow or an outline, for example) turns that property off when the action ends.

The Clip tab marks each row so you can see what the action touches:

| Mark | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ◆ | This action animates the row. The label turns strong and the field gets a border in the action colour. A popup, checkbox or other on/off control also shows "at end", because it switches rather than ramps |
| ◇ | Another action on the clip animates this row. Its tooltip names the action |
| ○ | The row follows a value this action animates (for example, Gain follows Volume) |
| ⊘ | Actions don't animate this row. Edits change the clip |

A slider on an animated row fills in the action colour from the value at the action's start to the knob. When the playhead is inside the clip, a coral tick shows the value at the playhead. A row that is a field only shows that value as a "now …" tag instead.

Section headers carry the same marks, and a section where every row is ⊘ says "Actions don't animate this. Edits here change the clip." Each sub-tab's label shows **◆N** when the selected action animates N of its keys. When you select an action, the sections it animates on the current sub-tab open automatically.

To take a property back out of an action:

- Hover over a ◆ and click the × that replaces it ("Remove from action N").
- Click **Clear** in a section's header to remove all of that section's keys from the action. While an action is selected and keys the section, Clear takes the place of the header's **Reset**; otherwise Reset shows only while the section differs from its defaults.
- Right-click a row for its menu: **Remove from action N** on an animated row, **Go to action M** on a ◇ row (selects that action), and **Set end value to default** (on a row the selected action animates) or **Reset to default** (otherwise). The default item is disabled when the row already holds its default.

*Agents:* `set_action_end` (a `patch` with `video`, `audio`, `text` and `graphic` groups and a top-level `speed`, merged into the end state; `null` removes a key; `off` lists `"group.key"` paths to switch off at the end). `video.motion` and `text.words` are refused.

### Move, resize and re-curve an action

**In the action lane or the timeline:**

- Drag a band's **body** to move the action within its clip.
- Drag a band's outer 5 pt (its grips, shown on hover) to move that end. A band 15 pt wide or narrower has no grips and only moves.

A drag snaps to whole frames, keeps the action at least one frame long, and stops at the neighbouring actions and the clip's ends. A dashed outline marks where the band started. A readout replaces the lane's header text: "start → end +s:ff" for a move or a start resize, "len +Nf" for an end resize. The whole drag is one undo step (**Move Action** or **Resize Action**). Dropping the band selects the action. Bands don't snap to the playhead or other edits. If Frame Job would refuse a position, the band just stops there.

**In the action lane's detail row** (shown while an action is selected):

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| Start | Where the action starts, as a timecode measured from the clip's start |
| Length | How long it takes, 0.01–36000 s (quick picks 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2) |
| Curve | Linear, In, Out or In Out, with a glyph of the curve beside it |
| Trash button | Removes the action |

When Frame Job refuses a typed Start or Length, or an end-state edit, the reason appears at the foot of the inspector as "Refused: …" with the rule's own sentence. It stays until the project next changes or you click it. A band drag never shows one.

*Agents:* `set_action` (`start`, `duration`, `curve`; any left out keep their value).

### Remove an action

With an action selected, press **⌫**, or click the trash button in the action lane. ⌫ removes only the action, not the clip.

Careful: **⌘⌫** (Ripple Delete) still ripple-deletes the whole selected clip, even while an action is selected.

A speed action can't be removed if doing so would make the clip read past the end of its media. The refusal names the latest clip end that fits. See [Speed](speed.md).

*Agents:* `remove_action`.

### Actions on the timeline

Each clip that has an action shows an **action lane** directly under its name strip, with one band per action. How much a band shows depends on **View ▸ Timeline Track Height**:

| Track height | A band shows |
|---|---|
| Small | The bar only |
| Medium | Its number, a zoom glyph for a zoom action, and the curve on the selected band |
| Large | All of that, plus the properties it changes (for example `scale, x, y`, or `speed`) |

Actions are numbered in time order, and the number is the same on the timeline and in the Clip tab. The selected action's band is solid, a wash runs down the clip under its span, and the span is shaded on the ruler.

### The action lane in the Clip tab

The Clip tab opens with a pinned block above its sections: the selection header, the action lane, and the sub-tabs. The action lane is a small timeline of the selected clip:

- **Header row:** ACTIONS, then the count (or "none") and "· editing N" while action N is selected, then three buttons: Zoom to Region (Z), Zoom Back, and Add Action (⌥⌘K).
- **Lane row:** the **Clip** chip (highlighted while no action is selected; click it to leave the action), then the whole clip with its actions as numbered bands and the playhead. Under the bands the lane also shows the clip's transition overlap (hatched), its audio fades and its motion wedges, the same marks the timeline draws. An empty lane reads "no actions · ⌥⌘K adds one".
- **Detail row:** only while an action is selected (see above).

With several clips selected the lane reads "Select one clip to edit its actions."

### How edits move actions

| Edit | What happens to the clip's actions |
|---|---|
| Trim the start | Actions keep their clip time, so they stay put relative to the clip's new start |
| Trim the end | Actions stay put, so one can end up running past the clip's new end; only the part inside the clip plays. You can still move it earlier, shorten it or change its curve, but not make it end any later |
| Slip or Roll | Actions stay where they are in clip time |
| Change the speed, or rate-stretch | Actions keep their place as a fraction of the clip |
| Split | Actions after the cut go to the second half; one that spans the cut is divided between the halves |
| Add a transition at a hard cut | The incoming clip's actions move with its new first frame, so a zoom stays on the frame it was drawn over |
| Duplicate, Copy and Paste | The copies keep their actions |
| Nest | The clips keep their actions inside the nest |
| Detach Audio | The new audio clip gets a copy of every action, so volume actions keep working |
| Freeze Frame | The still has no actions; the look at the frozen frame is baked into its own properties |
| Add Blurred Background | The backdrop copy has no actions, so a zoom on the foreground doesn't zoom the backdrop |
| Paste Attributes | Actions are not copied |

### On the timeline

A clip with an In or Out preset shows a small wedge along the bottom of its name strip, as long as the preset's duration at the current zoom. If the wedges overlap, the two presets are longer than the clip together. In that case Frame Job shortens both in proportion to their lengths, so the entrance ends on the frame where the exit begins, rather than refusing.

A clip with a During movement shows a small wave symbol at the right end of its name strip.

### Inactive presets

An In or Out with a zero duration can come from an agent or an older project. It is kept but does nothing. The section, the summary and the Motion menu mark it "(inactive)" (or "(some inactive)" across a selection), it draws no wedge, and a note reads "Selection includes inactive In motion (zero duration). Increase Duration to reactivate; choose None to clear."

### Limits

- A preset is not part of any action. Motion rows are ⊘, and edits always write the clip, even with an action selected.
- A split gives the first half no Out and the second half no In, so the cut doesn't play an exit and an entrance. A During movement restarts at each cut, so Remove Silences on a clip with Pulse or Drift can make it jump at the cuts.
- Freeze frame and Add Blurred Background drop the motion. Duplicate, Detach Audio and Paste keep it. Changing the speed doesn't rescale the presets.
- A text clip has no measured size, so a slide starts or ends half a canvas past the edge. That clears any text narrower than the canvas.
- A canvas drag started mid-motion starts from the clip's un-moved position.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`

  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting

  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

input.content:
---
title: "Action bands and the action lane"
description: "Read a clip's actions on the timeline and in the Clip tab, and use the action lane's buttons and fields to add, retime and remove them."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

An action shows up in two places: as a band on its clip in the timeline, and as a band in the action lane at the top of the Clip tab. Both are numbered the same way, and you can click or drag a band in either.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Add Action', 'View ▸ Timeline Track Height']}
  keys={['⌥⌘K', 'Z']}
  where={["Timeline, under a clip's name strip", 'Clip tab ▸ action lane']}
  tools={['add_action', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']}
/>

<Shot
  name="07b-clip-graphic-action.window"
  alt="The editor with a graphic clip and its one action selected. At the top of the Clip tab the action lane reads Actions 1, editing 1, with a solid band numbered 1 in the lane beside the Clip chip, and below it the detail row with 00:00:01:00, 2.00 s, Linear and a trash button. On the timeline the same band sits under the clip's name strip, a wash runs down the clip under its span, and the span is shaded on the ruler."
/>

## Bands on the timeline

A clip that has an action shows a lane directly under its name strip, with one band per action. Each band spans the action's time on the clip, and is at least 2 pt wide however short the action is.

Actions are numbered in time order, so a band's number is its place on the clip, and moving an action past another changes both numbers. The number is the same on the timeline and in the Clip tab.

Click a band to select the clip and that action. The playhead moves to the action's end, so the preview shows the state you're editing. Drag a band's body to move the action, or a grip to resize it. See [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/) and [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).

The selected action's band is solid. A wash runs down the clip under its span, and the span is shaded on the ruler.

A band on a locked track doesn't respond. It doesn't highlight, and clicking it selects the clip, not the action.

### Band detail by track height

How much a band shows depends on [**View ▸ Timeline Track Height**](/timeline/track-height/).

| Track height | Lane height | A band shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Small | 5 pt | A plain bar. |
| Medium | 12 pt | Its number, a zoom glyph for a zoom action, and the curve on the selected band. |
| Large | 18 pt | All of that, plus the properties it changes, such as `scale, x, y` or `speed`. A graphic's animated properties are listed with the clip's other properties. |

The zoom glyph is a small magnifier. It appears on any action that changes exactly scale, x and y, however the action was made.

From Medium, a clip whose rate moves also draws its rate line over the bands. While the line is there, a selected Speed band doesn't draw its curve. See [Speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/).

### Band hover

Point at a band, on the timeline or in the Clip tab's lane, and it brightens and shows a 5 pt grip at each end. The pointer is an open hand over the body and a resize arrow over a grip.

A band 15 pt wide or narrower has no grips, so you can only move it. On the timeline, zoom in to make it wider.

## The action lane in the Clip tab

The action lane is a small timeline of the selected clip. It's pinned at the top of the Clip tab, between the clip's name and the sub-tabs, so it stays put while you scroll the sections below. The whole clip always fits the lane's width, however long it is.

### Header row

The header reads **ACTIONS**, then the number of actions or "none". While action N is selected, it adds "· editing N". The three buttons at its right end are:

| Button | Tooltip | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Zoom-in magnifier | Zoom to Region (Z) | Lets you draw a rectangle on the canvas to zoom to. See [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/). |
| Zoom-out magnifier | Zoom Back | Adds an action that returns the clip to its own scale and position. See [Zoom Back](/motion/zoom-to-region/#zoom-back). |
| Plus | Add Action (⌥⌘K) | Adds an action at the playhead. See [Add an action](/motion/add-an-action/). |

While you drag a band in the lane, a readout takes the place of the header's text, with times counted from the clip's start. The buttons stay.

### Lane row

The **Clip** chip sits at the left. It's highlighted while no action is selected, and clicking it leaves the selected action, so the Clip tab goes back to editing the clip itself.

To its right is the whole clip, with its actions as numbered bands and the playhead as a thin line. Click or drag a band here as you would on the timeline. These bands show their number, the zoom glyph and the selected band's curve whatever the track height, and never list properties. A clip whose rate moves draws its rate line here too.

A clip with no actions shows "no actions · ⌥⌘K adds one".

### What else the lane shows

Under the bands, the lane draws the same marks the timeline draws for the clip, so you can place an action around them:

| Mark | Where | Shown when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hatching | At the clip's start | The clip has a [transition](/motion/transitions/) over a clip that's still running when it starts. |
| Fades | Triangles along the bottom, at either end | The clip has sound and a fade in or out. |
| Motion wedges | Triangles hanging from the top, at either end | The clip has an active In or Out [motion preset](/motion/motion-presets/). |

### Detail row

This row appears only while an action is selected. Each change is one undo step.

| Control | What it does | Range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start | Where the action starts, as a timecode measured from the clip's own start. | |
| Length | How long the action takes, in seconds, snapped to whole frames. | 0.01 to 36,000 s, with quick picks of 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 |
| Curve | How the action eases from its start to its end state, with a glyph of the curve beside it. | Linear, In, Out, In Out |
| Trash button | Removes the action. <kbd>⌫</kbd> does the same. | |

If Frame Job can't take a typed Start or Length, for example because the action would overlap another or run past the clip's end, it beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector, after "Refused:". The line stays until the project next changes or you click it.

### Several clips selected

With several clips selected the lane reads "Select one clip to edit its actions.", and there's no count, Clip chip, bands or detail row.

The three buttons stay. Add Action still works, and puts the action on the first selected clip under the playhead without selecting it. Zoom to Region and Zoom Back need a single clip, so they beep.

## The gutter mark

While an action is selected, each row of the Clip tab it animates has a ◆ in its left gutter. Hover over the ◆ and it turns into ×, with the tooltip "Remove from action N". Click it to take that row out of the action, as one undo step, Remove from Action. The row's right-click menu has the same command.

See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) for all the marks and what they mean.

## Related

- [Actions](/motion/actions/)
- [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/)
- [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/)
- [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/)
- [Track height](/timeline/track-height/)

input.content:
---
title: "How edits move actions"
description: "See what trimming, splitting, slipping, retiming, copying or freezing a clip does to its actions and its motion presets."
---

An action's times are measured from the clip's own start, not from the start of the timeline. So moving a clip takes its actions with it, but an edit that changes where the clip starts, how long it is or what it plays can change what an action lands on. This page goes through those edits one at a time.

## Trim

**Trimming the start** keeps each action's clip time. An action 2 s into the clip is still 2 s into the clip afterwards, so it stays put relative to the new start and now plays over different footage.

**Trimming the end** leaves actions where they are, so one can end up running past the clip's new end. A start trim shortens the clip too, so it can do the same.

Only the part of an action inside the clip plays, so a zoom cut off halfway stops partway in. You can still move that action earlier, shorten it or change its curve, but you can't make it end any later.

See [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/).

## Slip and roll

**Slip** and **Roll** leave actions where they are in clip time. A slip slides the footage under them. A roll moves the cut between two clips, and the actions on both stay put, as they do for a trim.

See [Slip and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/).

## Speed changes

Changing the speed, or rate-stretching with an <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag of the end edge, keeps each action at its place as a fraction of the clip. An action a quarter of the way through a clip is still a quarter of the way through, and it gets longer or shorter with the clip. **Clip ▸ Retime Range…** does the same in each clip it changes.

The times snap to whole frames, and an action is kept at least one frame long and inside the clip.

## Split

**Clip ▸ Split** (<kbd>⌘T</kbd>) shares the actions out between the two halves:

- An action that ends at or before the cut stays on the first half.
- An action that starts at or after the cut goes to the second half, with its times now counted from that half's start.
- An action that spans the cut is divided in two. The first piece ends at the values the action had reached at the cut, and the second carries on to the original end state.

Both pieces of a divided action keep its curve. The values match at the join, but an eased action can change pace there.

Adding a transition at a hard cut gives the incoming clip a new, earlier first frame. Its actions move with that frame, so a zoom stays on the frame it was drawn over.

**Edit ▸ Duplicate** (<kbd>⌘D</kbd>), an <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag, and **Edit ▸ Copy** then **Paste** all give copies that keep their actions, and the clip's name travels with them. Each copy's actions are its own, so changing one doesn't touch the other.

Clips you [nest](/editing/nests/) keep their actions inside the nest. Open the nest to see and edit them.

**Clip ▸ Detach Audio** (<kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd>) gives the new sound clip a copy of every action, so volume actions keep working. An action that only changes the picture does nothing on the sound clip.

The still that **Clip ▸ Freeze Frame** (<kbd>⇧⌘F</kbd>) makes has no actions. The backdrop copy that **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background** makes has no actions, so a zoom on the foreground doesn't zoom the backdrop.

| --- | --- |

## Related

- [Actions](/motion/actions/)
- [Action bands and the action lane](/motion/action-lane/)
- [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/)

---
title: "Zoom to Region"
description: "Draw a rectangle on the picture to zoom a clip to it, then pull back out with Zoom Back."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Zoom to Region is the screencast zoom: draw a rectangle on the picture, and the clip zooms until that rectangle fills the frame. The zoom is an ordinary [action](/motion/actions/), so you can retime it, change its curve or remove it like any other.

<AtAGlance
  keys="Z"
  where={['Clip tab ▸ action lane ▸ zoom-in magnifier (Zoom to Region)', 'Clip tab ▸ action lane ▸ zoom-out magnifier (Zoom Back)']}
  tools="add_zoom_action"
/>

## Zoom to Region

<Steps>

1. Select one clip and put the playhead where the zoom should start.

2. Press <kbd>Z</kbd>, or click the zoom-in magnifier in the [action lane](/motion/action-lane/). The pointer becomes a crosshair and a hint appears on the canvas.

3. Drag a rectangle over the canvas. It can start outside the picture, which helps when you want to catch the edge of the frame.

4. Release the mouse.

</Steps>

Frame Job adds a 1-second **Ease In Out** action at the playhead. Its end state is the scale and position that bring the rectangle to the canvas, worked out through the clip's rotation and crop as they are at that moment. It's one undo step, Zoom to Region.

The new action is selected, so you can go straight on to change its length or curve in the lane's [detail row](/motion/action-lane/#detail-row), or adjust where it ends with the [Clip tab's fields or the canvas](/motion/edit-an-action/).

The clip stays zoomed after the action ends, until a later action changes it. [Zoom Back](#zoom-back) is the way to pull out again.

## The canvas hint and outline

While the mode is on, a hint at the top of the canvas reads "Drag a rectangle to zoom to it · ⇧ fills · Esc to cancel".

As you drag, you see two outlines: the rectangle you're drawing, and a dimmer dashed one showing exactly what the canvas will show once the zoom lands. They differ when your rectangle isn't the shape of the canvas.

## Fit or fill

| To | Do this | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fit | Drag | The whole rectangle is shown. This is the default. |
| Fill | Hold <kbd>⇧</kbd> while dragging | The rectangle fills the canvas, and whatever doesn't match the canvas shape is cropped. |

Frame Job reads <kbd>⇧</kbd> at every step of the drag, so you can change your mind before you let go, and the dashed outline follows.

A zoom changes a clip's scale and position, never its angle. On a rotated clip, fit and fill are both measured through the rotation.

## Zoom Back

Zoom Back pulls the clip back out after a zoom.

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead past the end of the zoom, to where the pull-back should start. After Zoom to Region the playhead is still at the zoom's start, and a new action there would overlap it.

2. Click the zoom-out magnifier in the action lane.

</Steps>

Frame Job adds a 1-second **Ease In Out** action at the playhead whose end state is the clip's own base scale, x and y, whatever earlier actions did. There's no rectangle to draw and no key for it. The new action is selected, and it's one undo step, Zoom Back.

It needs the same clip as <kbd>Z</kbd>, and beeps otherwise.

## Which clip can be zoomed

<kbd>Z</kbd> and Zoom Back need exactly one selected clip that's drawn at the playhead and isn't on a locked track. Otherwise they beep. So they won't work with several clips selected, with the playhead off the clip, or on a sound-only clip.

The action also has to fit. Frame Job won't add a zoom that would overlap another action on the clip or run past the clip's end. It beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector, and a zoom you drew leaves the mode. Near the end of a clip, move the playhead back first or shorten an existing action.

## Leaving the mode

Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, press <kbd>Z</kbd> again, or click the button again. The mode also closes by itself when the selection changes or the playhead leaves the clip, and turning on another canvas tool, such as an eyedropper, ends it.

Once focus has left the canvas, for example after a click in the inspector, <kbd>Esc</kbd> no longer reaches the mode, and <kbd>Z</kbd> is the way out.

A rectangle under 6 canvas pixels wide or high, or a click with no drag, beeps and leaves the mode on so you can draw again.

## The scale limit

The zoom stops at 1,000 %, the largest scale a layer can take. The rectangle stays centred even then, but it doesn't reach the size you asked for. On a 1920-wide canvas, for example, a rectangle narrower than 192 pixels of the source picture can't fill the width.

## With a During preset

On a clip with a During [motion preset](/motion/during-presets/), a second hint appears under the first: "This clip has During motion — the zoom is solved without it". The zoom is worked out as if the preset weren't there, and the preset keeps moving the clip under the zoom, so the rectangle won't sit exactly in place.

The hint follows the clip, so it appears or goes if a During preset is added or cleared while the mode is on.

## Auto Zoom

To zoom a screen recording at every click at once, use **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…**. It plans these same zoom actions from the recording's cursor file. See [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/).

## Good to know

- You draw on the picture as it is at the playhead, with earlier actions applied, so you can draw a tighter zoom on a clip that's already zoomed.
- The rotation and crop are read at the start of the zoom. If you then animate either of them in the same action, the rectangle drifts across the action's span.

## With an agent

An agent gives the rectangle as numbers with `add_zoom_action` instead of drawing it, and can set the zoom's length and curve in the same call. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).

## Related

- [Add an action](/motion/add-an-action/)
- [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/)
- [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/)
- [Action bands and the action lane](/motion/action-lane/)
- [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/)

content.content:
# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history

---
title: "Action bands and the action lane"
description: "Read a clip's actions on the timeline and in the Clip tab, and use the action lane's buttons and fields to add, retime and remove them."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

An action shows up in two places: as a band on its clip in the timeline, and as a band in the action lane at the top of the Clip tab. Both are numbered the same way, and you can click or drag a band in either.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Add Action', 'View ▸ Timeline Track Height']}
  keys={['⌥⌘K', 'Z']}
  where={["Timeline, under a clip's name strip", 'Clip tab ▸ action lane']}
  tools={['add_action', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']}
/>

<Shot
  name="07b-clip-graphic-action.window"
  alt="The editor with a graphic clip and its one action selected. At the top of the Clip tab the action lane reads Actions 1, editing 1, with a solid band numbered 1 in the lane beside the Clip chip, and below it the detail row with 00:00:01:00, 2.00 s, Linear and a trash button. On the timeline the same band sits under the clip's name strip, a wash runs down the clip under its span, and the span is shaded on the ruler."
/>

## Bands on the timeline

A clip that has an action shows a lane directly under its name strip, with one band per action. Each band spans the action's time on the clip, and is at least 2 pt wide however short the action is.

Actions are numbered in time order, so a band's number is its place on the clip, and moving an action past another changes both numbers. The number is the same on the timeline and in the Clip tab.

Click a band to select the clip and that action. The playhead moves to the action's end, so the preview shows the state you're editing. Drag a band's body to move the action, or a grip to resize it. See [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/) and [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).

The selected action's band is solid. A wash runs down the clip under its span, and the span is shaded on the ruler.

A band on a locked track doesn't respond. It doesn't highlight, and clicking it selects the clip, not the action.

### Band detail by track height

How much a band shows depends on [**View ▸ Timeline Track Height**](/timeline/track-height/).

| Track height | Lane height | A band shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Small | 5 pt | A plain bar. |
| Medium | 12 pt | Its number, a zoom glyph for a zoom action, and the curve on the selected band. |
| Large | 18 pt | All of that, plus the properties it changes, such as `scale, x, y` or `speed`. A graphic's animated properties are listed with the clip's other properties. |

The zoom glyph is a small magnifier. It appears on any action that changes exactly scale, x and y, however the action was made.

From Medium, a clip whose rate moves also draws its rate line over the bands. While the line is there, a selected Speed band doesn't draw its curve. See [Speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/).

### Band hover

Point at a band, on the timeline or in the Clip tab's lane, and it brightens and shows a 5 pt grip at each end. The pointer is an open hand over the body and a resize arrow over a grip.

A band 15 pt wide or narrower has no grips, so you can only move it. On the timeline, zoom in to make it wider.

## The action lane in the Clip tab

The action lane is a small timeline of the selected clip. It's pinned at the top of the Clip tab, between the clip's name and the sub-tabs, so it stays put while you scroll the sections below. The whole clip always fits the lane's width, however long it is.

### Header row

The header reads **ACTIONS**, then the number of actions or "none". While action N is selected, it adds "· editing N". The three buttons at its right end are:

| Button | Tooltip | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Zoom-in magnifier | Zoom to Region (Z) | Lets you draw a rectangle on the canvas to zoom to. See [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/). |
| Zoom-out magnifier | Zoom Back | Adds an action that returns the clip to its own scale and position. See [Zoom Back](/motion/zoom-to-region/#zoom-back). |
| Plus | Add Action (⌥⌘K) | Adds an action at the playhead. See [Add an action](/motion/add-an-action/). |

While you drag a band in the lane, a readout takes the place of the header's text, with times counted from the clip's start. The buttons stay.

### Lane row

The **Clip** chip sits at the left. It's highlighted while no action is selected, and clicking it leaves the selected action, so the Clip tab goes back to editing the clip itself.

To its right is the whole clip, with its actions as numbered bands and the playhead as a thin line. Click or drag a band here as you would on the timeline. These bands show their number, the zoom glyph and the selected band's curve whatever the track height, and never list properties. A clip whose rate moves draws its rate line here too.

A clip with no actions shows "no actions · ⌥⌘K adds one".

### What else the lane shows

Under the bands, the lane draws the same marks the timeline draws for the clip, so you can place an action around them:

| Mark | Where | Shown when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hatching | At the clip's start | The clip has a [transition](/motion/transitions/) over a clip that's still running when it starts. |
| Fades | Triangles along the bottom, at either end | The clip has sound and a fade in or out. |
| Motion wedges | Triangles hanging from the top, at either end | The clip has an active In or Out [motion preset](/motion/motion-presets/). |

### Detail row

This row appears only while an action is selected. Each change is one undo step.

| Control | What it does | Range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start | Where the action starts, as a timecode measured from the clip's own start. | |
| Length | How long the action takes, in seconds, snapped to whole frames. | 0.01 to 36,000 s, with quick picks of 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 |
| Curve | How the action eases from its start to its end state, with a glyph of the curve beside it. | Linear, In, Out, In Out |
| Trash button | Removes the action. <kbd>⌫</kbd> does the same. | |

If Frame Job can't take a typed Start or Length, for example because the action would overlap another or run past the clip's end, it beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector, after "Refused:". The line stays until the project next changes or you click it.

### Several clips selected

With several clips selected the lane reads "Select one clip to edit its actions.", and there's no count, Clip chip, bands or detail row.

The three buttons stay. Add Action still works, and puts the action on the first selected clip under the playhead without selecting it. Zoom to Region and Zoom Back need a single clip, so they beep.

## The gutter mark

While an action is selected, each row of the Clip tab it animates has a ◆ in its left gutter. Hover over the ◆ and it turns into ×, with the tooltip "Remove from action N". Click it to take that row out of the action, as one undo step, Remove from Action. The row's right-click menu has the same command.

See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) for all the marks and what they mean.

## Related

- [Actions](/motion/actions/)
- [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/)
- [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/)
- [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/)
- [Track height](/timeline/track-height/)

---
title: "How edits move actions"
description: "See what trimming, splitting, slipping, retiming, copying or freezing a clip does to its actions and its motion presets."
---

An action's times are measured from the clip's own start, not from the start of the timeline. So moving a clip takes its actions with it, but an edit that changes where the clip starts, how long it is or what it plays can change what an action lands on. This page goes through those edits one at a time.

## Trim

**Trimming the start** keeps each action's clip time. An action 2 s into the clip is still 2 s into the clip afterwards, so it stays put relative to the new start and now plays over different footage.

**Trimming the end** leaves actions where they are, so one can end up running past the clip's new end. A start trim shortens the clip too, so it can do the same.

Only the part of an action inside the clip plays, so a zoom cut off halfway stops partway in. You can still move that action earlier, shorten it or change its curve, but you can't make it end any later.

See [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/).

## Slip and roll

**Slip** and **Roll** leave actions where they are in clip time. A slip slides the footage under them. A roll moves the cut between two clips, and the actions on both stay put, as they do for a trim.

See [Slip and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/).

## Speed changes

Changing the speed, or rate-stretching with an <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag of the end edge, keeps each action at its place as a fraction of the clip. An action a quarter of the way through a clip is still a quarter of the way through, and it gets longer or shorter with the clip. **Clip ▸ Retime Range…** does the same in each clip it changes.

The times snap to whole frames, and an action is kept at least one frame long and inside the clip.

See [Change a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/), [Rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/) and [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/). A clip with a speed ramp has its own rules, in [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/).

## Split

**Clip ▸ Split** (<kbd>⌘T</kbd>) shares the actions out between the two halves:

- An action that ends at or before the cut stays on the first half.
- An action that starts at or after the cut goes to the second half, with its times now counted from that half's start.
- An action that spans the cut is divided in two. The first piece ends at the values the action had reached at the cut, and the second carries on to the original end state.

Both pieces of a divided action keep its curve. The values match at the join, but an eased action can change pace there.

## Adding a transition

Adding a transition at a hard cut gives the incoming clip a new, earlier first frame. Its actions move with that frame, so a zoom stays on the frame it was drawn over.

When there's no spare footage and the incoming clip slides left to make the overlap instead, the clip moves whole and its actions go with it. See [Add or remove a transition](/motion/add-a-transition/).

## Duplicate, copy and paste

**Edit ▸ Duplicate** (<kbd>⌘D</kbd>), an <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag, and **Edit ▸ Copy** then **Paste** all give copies that keep their actions, and the clip's name travels with them. Each copy's actions are its own, so changing one doesn't touch the other.

Pasting into a project with a different frame rate snaps the actions' times to that project's frames.

See [Duplicate clips](/editing/duplicate-clips/) and [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/).

## Nest

Clips you [nest](/editing/nests/) keep their actions inside the nest. Open the nest to see and edit them.

## Detach Audio

**Clip ▸ Detach Audio** (<kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd>) gives the new sound clip a copy of every action, so volume actions keep working. An action that only changes the picture does nothing on the sound clip.

## Freeze Frame

The still that **Clip ▸ Freeze Frame** (<kbd>⇧⌘F</kbd>) makes has no actions. Instead, the look at the frozen frame is baked into the still's own properties: its position, scale, crop and anything an action had changed by that moment. So it lines up with the frame it froze, and holds there. See [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/).

## Add Blurred Background

The backdrop copy that **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background** makes has no actions, so a zoom on the foreground doesn't zoom the backdrop.

## Paste Attributes

**Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** (<kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>) doesn't copy actions. The clips you paste onto keep the actions they had. See [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/).

## What keeps or drops motion

[Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/) aren't actions, and they follow their own rules.

| Edit | What happens to the presets |
| --- | --- |
| Duplicate, Paste, Detach Audio | Kept. |
| Paste Attributes | Copied, with the rest of the clip's picture settings. |
| Freeze Frame | The still has none. It sits where the clip sits with no preset applied, so a freeze taken during an entrance can jump. |
| Add Blurred Background | The backdrop has none. The foreground keeps its own. |
| Split | The first half gives up its Out and the second half its In, so the cut doesn't play an exit and an entrance. During stays on both halves and restarts at the cut. |
| Change the speed | Kept, and not rescaled. |

Because During restarts at each cut, [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) on a clip with Pulse or Drift can make it jump at the cuts.

## Stale rows

Editing a graphic's module can leave an action naming a property that the module no longer declares, or no longer lets animate. With that action selected, the property shows as a dimmed row at the end of **Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Properties**, with its value and a **⌫** button. The tooltip says which of the two happened.

Click **⌫** to take the property out of the action. It's one undo step, Remove from Action. An agent does this with `set_action_end`, as described in [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).

See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).

## Related

- [Actions](/motion/actions/)
- [Action bands and the action lane](/motion/action-lane/)
- [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/)

---
title: "Zoom to Region"
description: "Draw a rectangle on the picture to zoom a clip to it, then pull back out with Zoom Back."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Zoom to Region is the screencast zoom: draw a rectangle on the picture, and the clip zooms until that rectangle fills the frame. The zoom is an ordinary [action](/motion/actions/), so you can retime it, change its curve or remove it like any other.

<AtAGlance
  keys="Z"
  where={['Clip tab ▸ action lane ▸ zoom-in magnifier (Zoom to Region)', 'Clip tab ▸ action lane ▸ zoom-out magnifier (Zoom Back)']}
  tools="add_zoom_action"
/>

## Zoom to Region

<Steps>

1. Select one clip and put the playhead where the zoom should start.

2. Press <kbd>Z</kbd>, or click the zoom-in magnifier in the [action lane](/motion/action-lane/). The pointer becomes a crosshair and a hint appears on the canvas.

3. Drag a rectangle over the canvas. It can start outside the picture, which helps when you want to catch the edge of the frame.

4. Release the mouse.

</Steps>

Frame Job adds a 1-second **Ease In Out** action at the playhead. Its end state is the scale and position that bring the rectangle to the canvas, worked out through the clip's rotation and crop as they are at that moment. It's one undo step, Zoom to Region.

The new action is selected, so you can go straight on to change its length or curve in the lane's [detail row](/motion/action-lane/#detail-row), or adjust where it ends with the [Clip tab's fields or the canvas](/motion/edit-an-action/).

The clip stays zoomed after the action ends, until a later action changes it. [Zoom Back](#zoom-back) is the way to pull out again.

## The canvas hint and outline

While the mode is on, a hint at the top of the canvas reads "Drag a rectangle to zoom to it · ⇧ fills · Esc to cancel".

As you drag, you see two outlines: the rectangle you're drawing, and a dimmer dashed one showing exactly what the canvas will show once the zoom lands. They differ when your rectangle isn't the shape of the canvas.

## Fit or fill

| To | Do this | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fit | Drag | The whole rectangle is shown. This is the default. |
| Fill | Hold <kbd>⇧</kbd> while dragging | The rectangle fills the canvas, and whatever doesn't match the canvas shape is cropped. |

Frame Job reads <kbd>⇧</kbd> at every step of the drag, so you can change your mind before you let go, and the dashed outline follows.

A zoom changes a clip's scale and position, never its angle. On a rotated clip, fit and fill are both measured through the rotation.

## Zoom Back

Zoom Back pulls the clip back out after a zoom.

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead past the end of the zoom, to where the pull-back should start. After Zoom to Region the playhead is still at the zoom's start, and a new action there would overlap it.

2. Click the zoom-out magnifier in the action lane.

</Steps>

Frame Job adds a 1-second **Ease In Out** action at the playhead whose end state is the clip's own base scale, x and y, whatever earlier actions did. There's no rectangle to draw and no key for it. The new action is selected, and it's one undo step, Zoom Back.

It needs the same clip as <kbd>Z</kbd>, and beeps otherwise.

## Which clip can be zoomed

<kbd>Z</kbd> and Zoom Back need exactly one selected clip that's drawn at the playhead and isn't on a locked track. Otherwise they beep. So they won't work with several clips selected, with the playhead off the clip, or on a sound-only clip.

The action also has to fit. Frame Job won't add a zoom that would overlap another action on the clip or run past the clip's end. It beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector, and a zoom you drew leaves the mode. Near the end of a clip, move the playhead back first or shorten an existing action.

## Leaving the mode

Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, press <kbd>Z</kbd> again, or click the button again. The mode also closes by itself when the selection changes or the playhead leaves the clip, and turning on another canvas tool, such as an eyedropper, ends it.

Once focus has left the canvas, for example after a click in the inspector, <kbd>Esc</kbd> no longer reaches the mode, and <kbd>Z</kbd> is the way out.

A rectangle under 6 canvas pixels wide or high, or a click with no drag, beeps and leaves the mode on so you can draw again.

## The scale limit

The zoom stops at 1,000 %, the largest scale a layer can take. The rectangle stays centred even then, but it doesn't reach the size you asked for. On a 1920-wide canvas, for example, a rectangle narrower than 192 pixels of the source picture can't fill the width.

## With a During preset

On a clip with a During [motion preset](/motion/during-presets/), a second hint appears under the first: "This clip has During motion — the zoom is solved without it". The zoom is worked out as if the preset weren't there, and the preset keeps moving the clip under the zoom, so the rectangle won't sit exactly in place.

The hint follows the clip, so it appears or goes if a During preset is added or cleared while the mode is on.

## Auto Zoom

To zoom a screen recording at every click at once, use **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…**. It plans these same zoom actions from the recording's cursor file. See [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/).

## Good to know

- You draw on the picture as it is at the playhead, with earlier actions applied, so you can draw a tighter zoom on a clip that's already zoomed.
- The rotation and crop are read at the start of the zoom. If you then animate either of them in the same action, the rectangle drifts across the action's span.

## With an agent

An agent gives the rectangle as numbers with `add_zoom_action` instead of drawing it, and can set the zoom's length and curve in the same call. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).

## Related

- [Add an action](/motion/add-an-action/)
- [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/)
- [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/)
- [Action bands and the action lane](/motion/action-lane/)
- [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/)

<system-reminder>
Contents of /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/help-docs/docs/site/CLAUDE.md:

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>
